translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 245.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 245 of the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀六十一】起閼逢攝提格，盡強圉大荒落，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 61] From Efeng Shetige through Qiangyu Dahuangluo; four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 61] From Efeng Shetige through Qiangyu Dahuangluo—four years in all.

sentences.zh: 文宗元聖昭獻孝皇帝中太和八年（

translations.literal: The eighth year of Taihe of Emperor Wenzong, Yuan Sheng Zhao Xian Filial Emperor, middle reign (
translations.idiomatic: The eighth year of Taihe in the middle reign of Emperor Wenzong, the Yuan Sheng Zhao Xian Filial Emperor (

sentences.zh: 甲寅，公元八三四年）

translations.literal: jiayin, corresponding to the year 834 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiayin, corresponding to 834 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，上疾小瘳。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Emperor's illness improved slightly.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the emperor's illness eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，御太和殿見近臣，然神識耗減，不能復故。

translations.literal: On dingsi, he attended the Taihe Hall to see close ministers, yet his mental faculties had diminished and could not return to their former state.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi he went to the Taihe Hall to receive his close ministers, but his mind had grown feeble and could not recover its former sharpness.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day renwu of the cycle, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the renwu new moon, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，丙戌，莒王紓薨。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, on bingxu, Prince Ju Shu died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, on bingxu, Prince Ju of Shu passed away.

sentences.zh: 上以久旱，詔求致雨之方。

translations.literal: Because of prolonged drought, the Emperor issued an edict seeking methods to bring rain.
translations.idiomatic: With the drought dragging on, the emperor issued an edict seeking ways to bring rain.

sentences.zh: 司門員外郎李中敏上表，以為：「仍歲大旱，非聖德不至，直以宋申錫之冤濫，鄭注之奸邪。

translations.literal: Li Zhongmin, Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, submitted a memorial stating: "Years of great drought are not because sagely virtue has failed to reach; it is simply due to the wrongful punishment of Song Shenxi and the treachery of Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: “Li Zhongmin, an assistant director in the Ministry of Justice, submitted a memorial arguing that the years of drought were not due to any lack of sagely virtue on the throne, but to the injustice done to Song Shenxi and the wickedness of Zheng Zhu.

sentences.zh: 今致雨之方，莫若斬注而雪申錫。」

translations.literal: The way to bring rain now is none better than executing Zhu and clearing Shenxi's name."
translations.idiomatic: The surest way to bring rain now would be to execute Zhu and vindicate Shenxi."

sentences.zh: 表留中。

translations.literal: The memorial was kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was held at court without action.

sentences.zh: 中敏謝病歸東都。

translations.literal: Zhongmin pleaded illness and returned to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmin pleaded illness and retired to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 郯王經薨。

translations.literal: Prince Tan Jing died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tan Jing passed away.

sentences.zh: 初，李仲言流象州，遇赦，還東都。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Zhongyan had been banished to Xiang Prefecture; on encountering an amnesty, he returned to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Zhongyan had been exiled to Xiang Prefecture; when an amnesty was declared, he returned to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 會留守李逢吉思復入相，仲言自言與鄭注善，逢吉使仲言厚賂之。

translations.literal: It happened that the eastern capital intendant Li Fengji wished to return as chief minister; Zhongyan said he was on good terms with Zheng Zhu, and Fengji had Zhongyan lavish gifts on him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eastern capital intendant Li Fengji was scheming to return to the chief ministership; Zhongyan claimed a close friendship with Zheng Zhu, and Fengji had him shower Zhu with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 注引仲言見王守澄，守澄薦於上，雲仲言善《易》，上召見之。

translations.literal: Zhu introduced Zhongyan to Wang Shoucheng; Shoucheng recommended him to the Emperor, saying Zhongyan was skilled in the Changes, and the Emperor summoned him for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu introduced Zhongyan to Wang Shoucheng, who recommended him to the emperor as a master of the Book of Changes; the emperor summoned him for an audience.

sentences.zh: 時仲言有母服，難入禁中，乃使衣民服，號王山人。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongyan was in mourning for his mother and could not easily enter the inner palace, so he was made to wear commoner's dress and was called Master Wang the Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan was then in mourning for his mother and could not readily enter the palace, so he wore civilian dress and went by the name Master Wang the Recluse.

sentences.zh: 仲言儀狀秀偉，倜儻尚氣，頗工文辭，有口辯，多權數。

translations.literal: Zhongyan was handsome and imposing in bearing, free-spirited and valuing honor, quite skilled in literary composition, eloquent in speech, and full of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan was tall and striking in appearance, bold and high-spirited, accomplished in letters, quick of tongue, and fertile in intrigue.

sentences.zh: 上見之，大悅，以為奇士，待遇日隆。

translations.literal: When the Emperor saw him, he was greatly pleased, regarded him as a remarkable man, and treated him with increasing favor day by day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took an immediate liking to him, judged him a man of rare talent, and lavished ever greater favor upon him.

sentences.zh: 仲言既除服，秋，八月，辛卯，上欲以仲言為諫言，置之翰林。

translations.literal: When Zhongyan's mourning was ended, in autumn, the eighth month, on xinmao, the Emperor wished to appoint Zhongyan remonstrance officer and place him in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongyan's mourning period ended, in autumn, the eighth month, on xinmao, the emperor wished to appoint him a remonstrance officer and place him in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 李德裕曰：「仲言向所為，計陛下必盡知之，豈宜置之近侍？」

translations.literal: Li Deyu said: "Zhongyan's past conduct—Your Majesty surely knows it all—how can he be placed among close attendants?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said, "Your Majesty must know full well what Zhongyan has done in the past—how can he be placed among your close attendants?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然豈不容其改過？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Yet should we not allow him to reform his faults?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Surely we can allow him to reform?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣聞惟顏回能不貳過。

translations.literal: He replied: "I have heard that only Yan Hui could avoid repeating a fault.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu replied, "I have heard that only Yan Hui never repeated a fault.

sentences.zh: 彼聖賢之過，但思慮不至，或失中道耳。

translations.literal: The faults of those sages and worthies were only failures of deliberation, or straying from the mean way.
translations.idiomatic: When sages err, it is only because their deliberation fell short or they strayed from the middle way.

sentences.zh: 至於仲言之惡，著於心本，安能悛改邪！」

translations.literal: As for Zhongyan's wickedness, it is rooted in his very heart—how could he repent and change!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan's wickedness is rooted in his very nature—how could he truly reform?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「李逢吉薦之，朕不欲食言。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Li Fengji recommended him; I do not wish to break my word."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Li Fengji recommended him, and I do not wish to go back on my word."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「逢吉身為宰相，乃薦奸邪以誤國，亦罪人也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Fengji, holding the post of chief minister, yet recommended a villain to mislead the state—he too is a guilty man."
translations.idiomatic: Deyu replied, "Fengji is chief minister, yet he recommended a villain to mislead the state—that too is a crime."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然則別除一官。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Then appoint him to some other office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then give him some other appointment."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「亦不可。」

translations.literal: He replied: "That too is not permissible."
translations.idiomatic: Deyu replied, "That too is out of the question."

sentences.zh: 上顧王涯，涯對曰：「可。」

translations.literal: The Emperor turned to Wang Ya; Ya replied: "It is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Wang Ya, who said, "That would be acceptable."

sentences.zh: 德裕揮手止之，上回顧適見，色殊不懌而罷。

translations.literal: Deyu waved his hand to stop him; the Emperor looked back just in time to see this, his expression most displeased, and the audience ended.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu gestured for him to stop; the emperor glanced back just then, his face dark with displeasure, and the audience broke up.

sentences.zh: 始，涯聞上欲用仲言，草諫疏極憤激；

translations.literal: At first, when Ya heard the Emperor wished to employ Zhongyan, he drafted a remonstrance of the utmost indignation;
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Ya heard the emperor meant to employ Zhongyan, he drafted a remonstrance burning with indignation;

sentences.zh: 既而見上意堅，且畏其黨盛，遂中變。

translations.literal: then, seeing the Emperor's resolve firm and fearing the strength of his faction, he changed course midway.
translations.idiomatic: but when he saw the emperor's resolve was firm and feared the power of Zhongyan's faction, he reversed himself midway.

sentences.zh: 尋以仲言為四門助教，給事中鄭肅、韓佽封還敕書。

translations.literal: Soon Zhongyan was appointed assistant instructor at the Four Gates; the Supervising Secretaries Zheng Su and Han Si returned the edict sealed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhongyan was appointed assistant instructor at the Four Gates College; the supervising secretaries Zheng Su and Han Si returned the edict unapproved.

sentences.zh: 德裕將出中書，謂涯曰：「且喜給事中封敕！」

translations.literal: As Deyu was about to leave the Secretariat, he said to Ya: "Rejoice—the supervising secretaries have sealed back the edict!"
translations.idiomatic: As Deyu was leaving the Secretariat, he told Ya, "Rejoice—the supervising secretaries have blocked the edict!"

sentences.zh: 涯即召肅、佽謂曰：「李公適留語，令二閣老不用封敕。」

translations.literal: Ya immediately summoned Su and Si and told them: "Lord Li just detained me with a message, instructing you two lords not to seal back the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Ya immediately summoned Su and Si and said, "Lord Li just detained me with word that you two gentlemen should not block the edict."

sentences.zh: 二人即行下，明日，以白德裕，德裕驚曰：「德裕不欲封還，當面聞，何必使人傳言！

translations.literal: The two at once carried it through; the next day they informed Deyu, who said in alarm: "Deyu did not wish it sealed back—he should have been told to my face; why send someone with a false message!
translations.idiomatic: The two at once let the edict pass; the next day they told Deyu, who exclaimed in alarm, "I never wanted the edict blocked—if you disagreed, tell me to my face! Why send someone with a false message?

sentences.zh: 且有司封駁，豈復稟宰相意邪！」

translations.literal: Besides, when the responsible offices seal back or reject, should they still take their cue from the chief minister's wishes!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, when the censorate blocks an edict, should it still defer to the chief minister's wishes?"

sentences.zh: 二人悵恨而去。

translations.literal: The two departed full of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The two left bitter and ashamed.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛亥，征昭義節度副使鄭注至京師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinhai, Zheng Zhu, deputy military commissioner of Zhaoyi, was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinhai, Zheng Zhu, deputy commissioner of Zhaoyi Circuit, was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 王守澄、李仲言、鄭注皆惡李德裕，以山南西道節度使李宗閔與德裕不相悅，引宗閔以敵之。

translations.literal: Wang Shoucheng, Li Zhongyan, and Zheng Zhu all hated Li Deyu; because Li Zongmin, military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, was at odds with Deyu, they brought in Zongmin to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng, Li Zhongyan, and Zheng Zhu all hated Li Deyu; knowing that Li Zongmin, commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, was Deyu's rival, they brought Zongmin in to counter him.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，詔征宗閔於興元。

translations.literal: On renxu, an edict summoned Zongmin from Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu an edict recalled Zongmin from Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛巳，幽州軍亂，逐節度使楊志誠及監軍李懷仵，推兵馬使史元忠主留務。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinsi, the Youzhou army mutinied, drove out Military Commissioner Yang Zhicheng and Army Supervisor Li Huaiwu, and installed the army inspector Shi Yuanzhong to manage the circuit's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinsi, the Youzhou garrison mutinied, expelled Commissioner Yang Zhicheng and army supervisor Li Huaiwu, and installed the army inspector Shi Yuanzhong as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以李宗閔為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Li Zongmin was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Li Zongmin was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent chief minister.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以中書侍郎、同平章事李德裕同平章事，充山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Li Deyu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Chief Minister, was retained as chief minister and appointed military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Li Deyu, vice director and concurrent chief minister, was sent out as military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit while retaining the chief ministership in title.

sentences.zh: 是日，以李仲言為翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: That same day, Li Zhongyan was appointed Hanlin Academician in Attendance and Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Li Zhongyan was appointed Hanlin lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 給事中高銖、鄭肅、韓佽、諫議大夫郭承嘏、中書舍人權璩等爭之，不能得。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretaries Gao Zhu, Zheng Su, and Han Si, Remonstrance Officer Guo Chenggu, and Secretariat Drafter Quan Ju and others protested but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries Gao Zhu, Zheng Su, and Han Si, remonstrance officer Guo Chenggu, and drafter Quan Ju protested in vain.

sentences.zh: 承嘏，晞之孫；

translations.literal: Chenggu was the grandson of Guo Xi;
translations.idiomatic: Chenggu was a grandson of Guo Xi;

sentences.zh: 璩，德輿之子也。

translations.literal: Ju was the son of Quan Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was a son of Quan Deyu.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，貢院奏進士複試詩賦，從之。

translations.literal: On yisi, the examination bureau memorialized that jinshi candidates be re-tested in poetry and rhapsody; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the examination bureau memorialized that jinshi candidates be re-tested in poetry and rhapsody; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 李德裕見上自陳，請留京師。

translations.literal: Li Deyu had an audience with the Emperor and pleaded to remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu had an audience and pleaded to remain in the capital.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以德裕為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Deyu was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Deyu was appointed minister of war.

sentences.zh: 楊志誠過太原，李載義自毆擊，欲殺之，幕僚諫救得免，殺其妻子及從行將卒。

translations.literal: As Yang Zhicheng passed through Taiyuan, Li Zaiyi personally beat him and tried to kill him; staff officers remonstrated and saved him, but his wife, children, and accompanying officers and soldiers were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Zhicheng passed through Taiyuan, Li Zaiyi attacked him personally and tried to kill him; staff officers intervened and saved Zhicheng, but his wife, children, and escort were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以載義有功，不問。

translations.literal: The court, because Zaiyi had rendered merit, did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The court took no action, since Zaiyi had rendered distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 載義母兄葬幽州，志誠發取其財。

translations.literal: Zaiyi's mother's elder brother had been buried in Youzhou; Zhicheng had his tomb opened and the property seized.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi's maternal uncle had been buried in Youzhou; Zhicheng had opened the tomb and seized the burial goods.

sentences.zh: 載義奏乞取志誠心以祭母，不許。

translations.literal: Zaiyi memorialized requesting Zhicheng's heart to sacrifice to his mother; permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi memorialized asking to take Zhicheng's heart as an offering for his mother; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 十一月，成德節度使王庭湊薨，軍中奉其子都知兵馬使元逵知留後。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Wang Tingcou, military commissioner of Chengde, died; the army installed his son, the army inspector Yuan Kui, as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Wang Tingcou, commissioner of Chengde, died; the army installed his son Yuan Kui, chief army inspector, as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元逵改父所為，事朝廷禮甚謹。

translations.literal: Yuan Kui reversed his father's conduct and observed court ritual with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Kui reversed his father's policies and treated the court with scrupulous deference.

sentences.zh: 史元忠獻楊志誠所造袞衣及諸僭物。

translations.literal: Shi Yuanzhong presented the imperial robes and other usurping regalia that Yang Zhicheng had made.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yuanzhong presented the imperial robes and other regalia of usurpation that Yang Zhicheng had had made.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，流志誠於嶺南，道殺之。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Zhicheng was banished to Lingnan and killed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Zhicheng was banished to Lingnan and killed en route.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔言李德裕制命已行，不宜自便。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin said that Li Deyu's appointment had already been issued and he ought not act on his own convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin argued that Deyu's commission had already been issued and he should not be allowed to choose his own posting.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，復以德裕為鎮海節度使，不復兼平章事。

translations.literal: On yihai, Deyu was again appointed military commissioner of Zhenhai, no longer concurrently chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Deyu was again sent out as commissioner of Zhenhai Circuit, stripped of the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 時德裕、宗閔各有朋黨，互相擠援。

translations.literal: At the time Deyu and Zongmin each had their factions, mutually undermining and supporting one another.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu and Zongmin each commanded a faction and worked ceaselessly to undermine the other.

sentences.zh: 上患之，每歎曰：「去河北賊易，去朝中朋黨難！」

translations.literal: The Emperor was troubled by this and often sighed: "Removing the bandits of Hebei is easy; removing the factions at court is hard!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was troubled and often sighed, "It is easy to drive out the rebels of Hebei, but hard to drive out the factions at court!"

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：「夫君子小人之不相容，猶水炭之不可同器而處也。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: "The mutual incompatibility of gentlemen and petty men is like water and fire, which cannot share one vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: "Gentlemen and petty men cannot coexist, any more than water and fire can share one vessel.

sentences.zh: 故君子得位則斥小人，小人得勢則排君子，此自然之理也。

translations.literal: Thus when gentlemen gain position they expel petty men; when petty men gain power they drive out gentlemen—this is the natural order.
translations.idiomatic: When gentlemen rise to office they drive out petty men; when petty men gain power they drive out gentlemen—that is the natural order of things.

sentences.zh: 然君子進賢退不肖，其處心也公，其指事也實；

translations.literal: Yet gentlemen advance the worthy and dismiss the unworthy; their hearts are public, their aims factual;
translations.idiomatic: Yet gentlemen promote the worthy and dismiss the unworthy; their hearts are impartial and their aims grounded in fact;

sentences.zh: 小人譽其所好，毀其所惡，其處心也私，其指事也誣。

translations.literal: petty men praise those they favor and slander those they hate; their hearts are private, their aims deceitful.
translations.idiomatic: petty men praise those they favor and slander those they hate; their hearts are selfish and their aims deceitful.

sentences.zh: 公且實者謂之正直，私且誣者謂之朋黨，在人主所以辨之耳。

translations.literal: What is public and factual is called uprightness; what is private and deceitful is called faction—it is for the ruler to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: What is impartial and true is called uprightness; what is selfish and false is called faction—it is for the ruler to tell them apart.

sentences.zh: 是以明主在上，度德而敘位，量能而授官；

translations.literal: Therefore when an enlightened ruler sits above, he measures virtue to rank men and gauges ability to grant office;
translations.idiomatic: An enlightened ruler measures men's virtue to rank them and gauges their ability to grant office;

sentences.zh: 有功者賞，有罪者刑；

translations.literal: those with merit are rewarded, those with guilt are punished;
translations.idiomatic: the meritorious are rewarded and the guilty punished;

sentences.zh: 奸不能惑，佞不能移。

translations.literal: the treacherous cannot beguile him, the sycophantic cannot sway him.
translations.idiomatic: the treacherous cannot beguile him and the sycophantic cannot sway him.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，則朋黨何自而生哉！

translations.literal: When it is so, from what could factions arise!
translations.idiomatic: When that is so, how could factions arise at all!

sentences.zh: 彼昏主則不然，明不能燭，強不能斷；

translations.literal: A benighted ruler is not so: his clarity cannot illuminate, his strength cannot decide;
translations.idiomatic: A benighted ruler is otherwise: his clarity cannot penetrate and his resolve cannot cut through;

sentences.zh: 邪正並進，毀譽交至；

translations.literal: the crooked and the straight advance together, slander and praise arrive in turn;
translations.idiomatic: the crooked and the straight advance together, slander and praise arrive in turn;

sentences.zh: 取捨不在於己，威福潛移於人。

translations.literal: choice and rejection are not in his own hands; authority and favor secretly shift to others.
translations.idiomatic: choice and rejection are no longer his own; power and favor quietly pass into others' hands.

sentences.zh: 於是讒慝得志，而朋黨之議興矣。

translations.literal: Then slanderers and villains have their way, and talk of factions arises.
translations.idiomatic: Then slanderers triumph and the talk of factions begins.

sentences.zh: 夫木腐而蠹生，醯酸而蚋集，故朝廷有朋黨，則人主當自咎，而不當以咎群臣也。

translations.literal: When wood rots, grubs breed; when vinegar turns sour, gnats gather—so when the court has factions, the ruler should blame himself, not reproach his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Rotten wood breeds worms; sour vinegar draws gnats—when factions arise at court, the ruler should blame himself, not his ministers.

sentences.zh: 文宗苟患群臣之朋黨，何不察其所毀譽者為實，為誣；

translations.literal: If Emperor Wenzong truly grieved at his ministers' factions, why did he not examine whether their praise and blame were factual or false;
translations.idiomatic: If Wenzong truly grieved over factionalism, why did he not examine whether their praise and blame were true or false,

sentences.zh: 所進退者為賢，為不肖；

translations.literal: whether those they advanced or dismissed were worthy or unworthy;
translations.idiomatic: whether those they advanced or dismissed were worthy or unworthy,

sentences.zh: 其心為公，為私；

translations.literal: whether their hearts were public or private;
translations.idiomatic: whether their hearts were public or private,

sentences.zh: 其人為君子，為小人！

translations.literal: whether the men themselves were gentlemen or petty men!
translations.idiomatic: whether the men themselves were gentlemen or petty men!

sentences.zh: 苟實也，賢也，公也，君子也，匪徒用其言，又當進之；

translations.literal: If factual, worthy, public, and gentlemen, he should not only heed their words but promote them;
translations.idiomatic: If their words were true, their men worthy, their hearts public, and they themselves gentlemen, he should not only heed them but promote them;

sentences.zh: 誣也，不肖也，私也，小人也，匪徒棄其言，又當刑之。

translations.literal: if false, unworthy, private, and petty men, he should not only reject their words but punish them.
translations.idiomatic: if false, unworthy, private, and petty, he should not only reject their words but punish them.

sentences.zh: 如是，雖使之為朋黨，孰敢哉！

translations.literal: Were it so, even if one bade them form factions, who would dare!
translations.idiomatic: Had he done so, who would have dared form factions even if invited!

sentences.zh: 釋是不為，乃怨群臣之難治，是猶不種不芸而怨田之蕪也。

translations.literal: He set this aside and did not do it, yet blamed his ministers as hard to govern—this is like neither sowing nor weeding yet blaming the field for weeds.
translations.idiomatic: He neglected this and then complained that his ministers were hard to govern—as if one neither sowed nor weeded yet blamed the field for going wild.

sentences.zh: 朝中之黨且不能去，況河北賊乎！」

translations.literal: He could not even remove the factions at court—how much less the bandits of Hebei!"
translations.idiomatic: He could not even purge the factions at court—how could he hope to drive out the rebels of Hebei!"

sentences.zh: 丙子，李仲言請改名訓。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Li Zhongyan requested to change his name to Xun.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Li Zhongyan petitioned to change his name to Xun.

sentences.zh: 幽州奏莫州軍亂，刺史張元泛不知所在。

translations.literal: Youzhou reported that the Mo Prefecture army had mutinied and Prefect Zhang Yuanfan's whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou reported a mutiny in Mo Prefecture; Prefect Zhang Yuanfan's whereabouts were unknown.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙卯，以昭義節度副使鄭注為太僕卿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Zheng Zhu, deputy military commissioner of Zhaoyi, was appointed Grand Master of Studs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Zheng Zhu, deputy commissioner of Zhaoyi, was appointed grand master of studs.

sentences.zh: 郭承嘏累上疏言其不可，上不聽。

translations.literal: Guo Chenggu repeatedly submitted memorials saying this was impermissible; the Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chenggu repeatedly memorialized against the appointment; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 於是注詐上表固辭，上遣中使再以告身賜之，不受。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhu feigned a memorial firmly declining; the Emperor sent a palace envoy to present the commission of appointment again, but Zhu would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu then feigned a memorial firmly declining; the emperor sent a palace envoy to present the commission again, but Zhu refused it.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以史元忠為盧龍留後。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Shi Yuanzhong was appointed acting commissioner of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Shi Yuanzhong was confirmed as acting commissioner of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 初，宋申錫與御史中丞宇文鼎受密詔誅鄭注，使京兆尹王璠掩捕之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Song Shenxi and Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Ding had received a secret edict to execute Zheng Zhu and ordered Metropolitan Magistrate Wang Fan to seize him by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Song Shenxi and censor-in-chief Yuwen Ding had received a secret edict to kill Zheng Zhu and ordered the metropolitan magistrate Wang Fan to seize him by surprise.

sentences.zh: 璠密以堂帖示王守澄，注由是得免，深德璠。

translations.literal: Fan secretly showed the office order to Wang Shoucheng; Zhu thereby escaped and was deeply grateful to Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan secretly showed the arrest order to Wang Shoucheng; Zhu thus escaped and was deeply indebted to Fan.

sentences.zh: 璠又與李訓善，於是訓、注共薦之，自浙西觀察使征為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Fan was also on good terms with Li Xun; thereupon Xun and Zhu jointly recommended him, and he was summoned from observer of Zhexi to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was also close to Li Xun; Xun and Zhu jointly recommended him, and he was recalled from Zhexi to vice director of the left department of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 文宗元聖昭獻孝皇帝中太和九年（

translations.literal: The ninth year of Taihe of Emperor Wenzong, Yuan Sheng Zhao Xian Filial Emperor, middle reign (
translations.idiomatic: The ninth year of Taihe in the middle reign of Emperor Wenzong, the Yuan Sheng Zhao Xian Filial Emperor (

sentences.zh: 乙卯，公元八三五年）

translations.literal: yimao, corresponding to the year 835 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yimao, corresponding to 835 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙卯，以王元逵為成德節度使。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yimao, Wang Yuankui was appointed military commissioner of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yimao, Wang Yuankui was made military commissioner of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 巢公湊薨，追贈齊王。

translations.literal: Duke of Chao Gong Cou died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Chao Gong Cou passed away and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 鄭注上言秦地有災，宜興役以禳之。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu memorialized that the Qin region had suffered disaster and that corvée labor should be undertaken to avert it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu submitted a memorial saying that calamity had struck the Qin region and that public works should be launched to ward it off.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，發左、右神策千五百人浚曲江及昆明池。

translations.literal: On xinmao, one thousand five hundred men from the Left and Right Shence Armies were dispatched to dredge the Qujiang and the Kunming Pool.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, fifteen hundred troops from the Left and Right Shence Armies were sent to dredge the Qujiang and the Kunming Pool.

sentences.zh: 三月，冀王絿薨。

translations.literal: In the third month, Prince of Ji Kui died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Prince of Ji Kui passed away.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以史元忠為盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Shi Yuanzhong was appointed military commissioner of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Shi Yuanzhong was made military commissioner of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 初，李德裕為浙西觀察使，漳王傅母杜仲陽坐宋申錫事放歸金陵，詔德裕存處之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Li Deyu was observation commissioner of Zhexi, the wet nurse of the Prince of Zhang, Du Zhongyang, implicated in the Song Shenxi affair, was released to Jinling; an edict ordered Deyu to support and provide for her.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Li Deyu was observation commissioner of Zhexi, the Prince of Zhang's wet nurse Du Zhongyang had been sent home to Jinling for her involvement in the Song Shenxi case, and the court ordered Deyu to see to her upkeep.

sentences.zh: 會德裕已離浙西，牒留後李蟾使如詔旨。

translations.literal: It happened that Deyu had already left Zhexi; he sent a dispatch to the acting commissioner Li Chan to carry out the edict as instructed.
translations.idiomatic: By then Deyu had already left Zhexi, so he sent instructions to the acting commissioner Li Chan to carry out the edict.

sentences.zh: 至是，左承王璠、戶部侍郎李漢奏德裕厚賂仲陽，陰結漳王，圖為不軌。

translations.literal: At this time, the Left Vice Director Wang Fan and the Vice Minister of Revenue Li Han memorialized that Deyu had lavishly bribed Zhongyang, secretly allied with the Prince of Zhang, and plotted sedition.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture, Vice Director Wang Fan and Vice Minister of Revenue Li Han accused Deyu of bribing Zhongyang heavily, secretly cultivating ties with the Prince of Zhang, and plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 上怒甚，召宰相及璠、漢、鄭注等面質之。

translations.literal: The emperor was exceedingly angry and summoned the chancellors together with Fan, Han, Zheng Zhu, and others to confront them face to face.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and summoned the chancellors along with Fan, Han, Zheng Zhu, and the others to confront them in person.

sentences.zh: 璠、漢等極口誣之，路隋曰：「德裕不至有此。

translations.literal: Fan, Han, and the rest slandered him to the utmost; Lu Sui said, "Deyu would not go so far as this.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, Han, and the others heaped slander upon him, but Lu Sui said, "Deyu would never do such a thing.

sentences.zh: 果如所言，臣亦應得罪！」

translations.literal: If it is truly as stated, your subject too ought to be guilty!"
translations.idiomatic: If what you say is true, then I too ought to be punished!"

sentences.zh: 言者稍息。

translations.literal: The speakers gradually quieted.
translations.idiomatic: The accusers gradually fell silent.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以德裕為賓客分司。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Deyu was made honorary guest of the crown prince with a separate office.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Deyu was demoted to honorary guest of the crown prince with a separate office.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以鄭注守太僕卿，兼御史大夫，注始受之，仍舉倉部員外郎李款自代曰：「加臣之罪，雖於理而無辜；

translations.literal: On guisi, Zheng Zhu was appointed acting Grand Master of Splendid Horses, concurrently Censor-in-Chief; Zhu accepted for the first time and still recommended Li Kuan, an assistant in the Bureau of Granaries, to replace him, saying, "To add to your subject's guilt, though by reason he is innocent;
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Zheng Zhu was appointed acting Grand Master of Splendid Horses and concurrent Censor-in-Chief; Zhu accepted at last and still nominated Li Kuan of the Bureau of Granaries to succeed him, saying, "If you heap guilt upon me, though I am innocent by rights,

sentences.zh: 在款之誠，乃事君而盡節。」

translations.literal: in Kuan's sincerity lies service to the ruler with utmost devotion."
translations.idiomatic: in Kuan's loyalty lies service to the throne with utmost devotion."

sentences.zh: 時人皆哂之。

translations.literal: People of the time all sneered at him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries all laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以門下侍郎、同平章事路隋同平章事，充鎮海節度使，趣之赴鎮，不得面辭。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Lu Sui, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor, was made Associate Grand Councillor and military commissioner of Zhenhai; he was urged to proceed to his post and was not permitted a farewell audience.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Lu Sui, vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand councillor, was sent out as military commissioner of Zhenhai and ordered to take up his post at once without a parting audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 坐救李德裕故也。

translations.literal: This was because he had defended Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: This was punishment for having spoken up for Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 初，京兆尹河南賈餗，性褊躁輕率，與李德裕有隙，而善於李宗閔、鄭注。

translations.literal: Initially, Jia Su of Henan, metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, was by nature narrow-minded, impetuous, and rash; he bore a grudge against Li Deyu but was on good terms with Li Zongmin and Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Su of Henan, the metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, was narrow-minded, impetuous, and rash; he was at odds with Li Deyu but close to Li Zongmin and Zheng Zhu.

sentences.zh: 上巳，賜百官宴於曲江，故事，尹於外門下馬，揖御史。

translations.literal: On the Shangsi festival, the emperor granted the hundred officials a banquet at the Qujiang; by precedent, the metropolitan magistrate dismounted at the outer gate and bowed to the censors.
translations.idiomatic: On the Shangsi festival the court gave the officials a banquet at the Qujiang; by custom the metropolitan magistrate was to dismount at the outer gate and bow to the censors.

sentences.zh: 餗恃其貴勢，乘馬直入，殿中侍御史楊儉、蘇特與之爭，餗罵曰：「黃面兒敢爾！」

translations.literal: Su relied on his exalted power and rode his horse straight in; the palace censors Yang Jian and Su Te disputed with him, and Su cursed, "Yellow-faced brats dare do this!"
translations.idiomatic: Relying on his lofty status, Su rode straight through; palace censors Yang Jian and Su Te challenged him, and Su shouted, "You yellow-faced pups dare behave like this!"

sentences.zh: 坐罰俸。

translations.literal: He was punished by reduction of salary.
translations.idiomatic: He was fined a portion of his salary.

sentences.zh: 餗恥之，求出，詔以為浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: Ashamed, Su sought a transfer out; an edict appointed him observation commissioner of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Su asked to leave the capital and was appointed observation commissioner of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 尚未行，戊戌，以餗為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Before he had departed, on wuxu he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, on wuxu he was made vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 庚子，制以曏日上初得疾，王涯呼李德裕奔問起居，德裕竟不至。

translations.literal: On gengzi, an edict stated that on a previous day when the emperor had first fallen ill, Wang Ya had summoned Li Deyu to rush and inquire after his health, yet Deyu ultimately did not come.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi an edict declared that when the emperor had first fallen ill some days before, Wang Ya had called on Li Deyu to hurry and inquire after him, but Deyu had never come.

sentences.zh: 又在西蜀征逋懸錢三十萬緡，百姓愁困。

translations.literal: Moreover, in western Shu he had collected three hundred thousand strings in overdue taxes, and the common people were distressed and impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: He had also levied three hundred thousand strings in back taxes in western Shu, leaving the people in misery.

sentences.zh: 貶德裕袁州長史。

translations.literal: Deyu was demoted to administrator of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was demoted to administrator of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，宋申錫獲罪，宦官益橫。

translations.literal: Initially, after Song Shenxi was condemned, the eunuchs grew ever more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: After Song Shenxi's downfall, the eunuchs had grown ever more domineering.

sentences.zh: 上外雖包容，內不能堪。

translations.literal: Outwardly the emperor seemed tolerant, but inwardly he could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly the emperor seemed to tolerate them, but inwardly he could endure it no longer.

sentences.zh: 李訓、鄭注既得幸，揣知上意，訓因進講，數以微言動上。

translations.literal: After Li Xun and Zheng Zhu had gained favor, they divined the emperor's intent; Xun, through his lectures, several times used subtle words to move the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Xun and Zheng Zhu had won the emperor's favor, they sensed his true mind; Xun, in his lectures, repeatedly nudged him with veiled hints.

sentences.zh: 上見其才辯，意訓可與謀大事，且以訓、注皆因王守澄以進，冀宦官不之疑，遂密以誠告之。

translations.literal: The emperor saw his eloquence and judged that Xun could be enlisted for great undertakings; moreover, because both Xun and Zhu had advanced through Wang Shoucheng, he hoped the eunuchs would not suspect them, and so confided his true intent to them in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by his eloquence, the emperor decided Xun could help him with a great design; since both Xun and Zhu had risen through Wang Shoucheng, he hoped the eunuchs would not suspect them, and confided his true purpose to them in secret.

sentences.zh: 訓、注遂以誅宦官為己任，二人相挾，朝夕計議，所言於上無不從，聲勢炟赫。

translations.literal: Xun and Zhu thereupon took the execution of the eunuchs as their own charge; the two supported each other, planning morning and evening; whatever they said to the emperor was never refused, and their power and renown blazed brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Zhu then made the destruction of the eunuchs their mission; backing each other, they plotted day and night, and nothing they proposed was refused; their power and fame blazed.

sentences.zh: 注多在禁中，或時休沐，賓客填門，賂遺山積。

translations.literal: Zhu was often in the inner palace; when he occasionally took rest days, guests filled his gate and bribes piled like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu spent much of his time in the inner palace; on his rare days off, visitors packed his gate and gifts piled up like hills.

sentences.zh: 外人但知訓、注倚宦官擅作威福，不知其與上有密謀也。

translations.literal: Outsiders only knew that Xun and Zhu relied on the eunuchs to arrogate power and privilege; they did not know of their secret conspiracy with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The world only saw Xun and Zhu leaning on the eunuchs to lord it over others; no one knew they were in secret league with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上之立也，右領軍將軍興寧仇士良有功。

translations.literal: When the emperor was established on the throne, Qiu Shiliang of Xingning, Right Army General, had rendered merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, the Right Army General Qiu Shiliang of Xingning had done him a great service.

sentences.zh: 王守澄抑之，由是有隙。

translations.literal: Wang Shoucheng had suppressed him, and thereby a rift arose.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng had held him down, and bad blood grew between them.

sentences.zh: 訓、注為上謀，進擢士良以分守澄之權。

translations.literal: Xun and Zhu plotted for the emperor and promoted Shiliang to divide Shoucheng's power.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Zhu advised the emperor to promote Shiliang in order to split Shoucheng's authority.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙丑，以士良為左神策中尉，守澄不悅。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yichou, Shiliang was made Left Shence Commandant; Shoucheng was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yichou, Shiliang was appointed Left Shence Commandant, to Shoucheng's displeasure.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以左丞王璠為戶部尚書、判度支。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the Left Vice Director Wang Fan was made Minister of Revenue and concurrent controller of fiscal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Vice Director Wang Fan was appointed minister of revenue and put in charge of fiscal affairs.

sentences.zh: 京城訛言鄭注為上合金丹，須小兒心肝，民間驚懼，上聞而惡之。

translations.literal: A rumor spread through the capital that Zheng Zhu was compounding an elixir of immortality for the emperor and needed the hearts and livers of children; the populace was alarmed and fearful, and when the emperor heard of it he detested it.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors swept the capital that Zheng Zhu was refining an elixir of immortality for the emperor and required children's hearts and livers; the people were terrified, and the emperor was revolted when he heard of it.

sentences.zh: 鄭注素惡京兆尹楊虞卿，與李訓共構之，雲此語出於虞卿家人。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu had long hated the metropolitan magistrate Yang Yuqing; together with Li Xun he framed him, saying this talk had come from Yuqing's household.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu had long hated the metropolitan magistrate Yang Yuqing; he and Li Xun framed him together, claiming the rumor had originated in Yuqing's household.

sentences.zh: 上怒，六月，下虞卿御史獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; in the sixth month, Yuqing was cast into the censorate prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, and in the sixth month Yuqing was thrown into the censorate prison.

sentences.zh: 注求為兩省官，中書侍郎、同平章事李宗閔不許，注毀之於上。

translations.literal: Zhu sought an office in the two central departments; the Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor Li Zongmin would not permit it, and Zhu slandered him to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu sought a post in the Secretariat or Chancellery, but Vice Director Li Zongmin, associate grand councillor, refused; Zhu then maligned him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會宗閔救楊虞卿，上怒，叱出之。

translations.literal: When Zongmin came to Yang Yuqing's rescue, the emperor was angry and shouted him out.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongmin tried to save Yang Yuqing, the emperor erupted and drove him from the hall.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，貶明州刺史。

translations.literal: On renyin, he was demoted to prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he was demoted to prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 左神策中尉韋元素、樞密使楊承和、王踐言久居中用事，與王守澄爭權不葉，李訓、鄭注因之出承和於西川，元素於淮南，踐言於河東，皆為監軍。

translations.literal: The Left Shence Commandant Wei Yuansu and the Military Affairs Commissioners Yang Chenghe and Wang Jianyan had long held power at court; they vied with Wang Shoucheng for authority and were not harmonious; Li Xun and Zheng Zhu took advantage of this to send Chenghe to western Shu, Yuansu to Huainan, and Jianyan to Hedong, all as army supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Shence Commandant Wei Yuansu and the military affairs commissioners Yang Chenghe and Wang Jianyan had long wielded power at court and clashed with Wang Shoucheng; Li Xun and Zheng Zhu used this to send Chenghe to western Shu, Yuansu to Huainan, and Jianyan to Hedong, each as army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲辰朔，貶楊虞卿虔州司馬。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the jiachen new moon, Yang Yuqing was demoted to aide of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the jiachen new moon, Yang Yuqing was demoted to aide of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，作紫雲樓於曲江。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Ziyun Tower was built at the Qujiang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the Ziyun Tower was erected at the Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以御史大夫李固言為門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Censor-in-Chief Li Guyin was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Censor-in-Chief Li Guyin was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 李訓、鄭注為上畫太平之策，以為當先除宦官，次復河、湟，次清河北，開陳方略，如指諸掌。

translations.literal: Li Xun and Zheng Zhu drew up for the emperor a strategy for great peace, holding that the eunuchs should first be eliminated, next the He and Huang regions recovered, next the area north of the Yellow River in Hebei pacified; they laid out their plans as if pointing at their palms.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun and Zheng Zhu outlined for the emperor a plan for an age of peace: first destroy the eunuchs, then recover the He and Huang frontier, then pacify Hebei north of the Yellow River; they unfolded their strategy as clearly as if it lay in the palm of the hand.

sentences.zh: 上以為信然，寵任日隆。

translations.literal: The emperor believed it trustworthy, and their favor and trust grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took them at their word, and their favor and authority rose day by day.

sentences.zh: 初，李宗閔為吏部侍郎，因附馬都尉沈結女學士宋若憲、知樞密楊承和得為相。

translations.literal: Initially, when Li Zongmin was Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, through the Princess Consort of Shen's connection to the female academician Song Ruoxian and the military affairs commissioner Yang Chenghe he had become chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Li Zongmin was vice minister of personnel, he had become chancellor through the Princess Consort of Shen's ties to the female academician Song Ruoxian and the military affairs commissioner Yang Chenghe.

sentences.zh: 及貶明州，鄭注發其事，壬子，再貶處州長史。

translations.literal: When he was demoted to Mingzhou, Zheng Zhu exposed the affair; on renzi he was demoted again to administrator of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his demotion to Mingzhou, Zheng Zhu exposed the affair; on renzi he was demoted again to administrator of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 著作郎、分司舒元輿與李訓善，訓用事，召為右司郎中，兼侍御史知雜，鞫楊虞卿獄。

translations.literal: Shu Yuanyu, an author at the court and holder of a separate office, was friendly with Li Xun; when Xun came to power he was summoned as Director of the Right Directorate and concurrently attendant censor administering miscellaneous matters, to try the case of Yang Yuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Yuanyu, a drafting officer on detached duty, was close to Li Xun; once Xun was in power he summoned him as director in the Right Directorate and concurrent attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous cases to prosecute Yang Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，擢為御史中丞。

translations.literal: On guichou, he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 元輿，元褒之兄也。

translations.literal: Yuanyu was the elder brother of Yuan Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu was the elder brother of Yuan Bao.

sentences.zh: 貶吏部侍郎李漢為汾州刺史，刑部侍郎蕭浣為遂州刺史，皆坐李宗閔之黨。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister of Personnel Li Han was demoted to prefect of Fenzhou, and the Vice Minister of Punishments Xiao Huan to prefect of Suizhou; both were punished as members of Li Zongmin's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Li Han was demoted to prefect of Fenzhou and Vice Minister of Punishments Xiao Huan to prefect of Suizhou, both as partisans of Li Zongmin.

sentences.zh: 是時李訓、鄭注連逐三相，威震天下，於是平生絲恩發怨無不報者。

translations.literal: At this time Li Xun and Zheng Zhu had in succession driven out three chancellors, and their awe shook the realm; then every thread of favor and flash of resentment from their lifetimes was repaid without exception.
translations.idiomatic: By then Li Xun and Zheng Zhu had driven out three chancellors in a row, and their power awed the empire; every old kindness and slight was now settled.

sentences.zh: 李訓奏僧尼猥多，耗蠹公私。

translations.literal: Li Xun memorialized that monks and nuns were excessively numerous and drained public and private resources.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun reported that monks and nuns had grown too numerous and were draining the public and private purse.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，詔所在試僧尼誦經不中格者，皆勒歸俗。

translations.literal: On dingsi, an edict ordered that wherever monks and nuns were tested in sutra recitation and failed the standard, they were all compelled to return to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi an edict ordered that monks and nuns who failed sutra examinations were to be forced back into lay life.

sentences.zh: 禁置寺及私度人。

translations.literal: The founding of temples and private ordinations were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: The building of new temples and private ordinations were banned.

sentences.zh: 時人皆言鄭注朝夕且為相，侍御史李甘揚言於朝曰：「白麻出，我必壞之於庭！」

translations.literal: People of the time all said that Zheng Zhu would soon become chancellor morning or evening; the attendant censor Li Gan proclaimed at court, "When the white hemp edict comes forth, I shall surely tear it apart in the courtyard!"
translations.idiomatic: Everyone said Zheng Zhu would be made chancellor any day now; Attendant Censor Li Gan declared at court, "The moment the white hemp appointment appears, I will tear it to pieces in the courtyard!"

sentences.zh: 癸亥，貶甘封州司馬。

translations.literal: On guihai, Gan was demoted to aide of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Li Gan was demoted to aide of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 然李訓亦忌注，不欲使為相，事竟寢。

translations.literal: Yet Li Xun also was jealous of Zhu and did not wish him to become chancellor; the matter was ultimately shelved.
translations.idiomatic: But Li Xun too resented Zhu and did not want him made chancellor, and in the end the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以國子博士李訓為兵部郎中、知制誥，依前侍講學士。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the National University Doctor Li Xun was made Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and drafter of edicts, continuing as before as attendant lecture academician.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, National University lecturer Li Xun was appointed director in the Bureau of Military Affairs and drafter of edicts, while retaining his post as attendant lecture academician.

sentences.zh: 貶左金吾大將軍沈為邵州刺史。

translations.literal: The Left Golden Crow General Shen was demoted to prefect of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Left Golden Crow General Shen was demoted to prefect of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙子，又貶李宗閔潮州司戶，賜宋若憲死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingzi, Li Zongmin was demoted again to registrar of Chaozhou, and Song Ruoxian was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingzi, Li Zongmin was demoted again to registrar of Chaozhou, and Song Ruoxian was ordered to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以太僕卿鄭注為工部尚書，充翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: On dingchou, the Grand Master of Splendid Horses Zheng Zhu was made Minister of Works and attendant Hanlin lecture academician.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Grand Master of Splendid Horses Zheng Zhu was appointed minister of works and Hanlin attendant lecture academician.

sentences.zh: 注好服鹿裘，以隱淪自處，上以師友待之。

translations.literal: Zhu liked to wear a deerskin coat and presented himself as a recluse; the emperor treated him as teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu favored deerskin robes and styled himself a recluse; the emperor treated him as teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 注之初得幸，上嘗問翰林學士、戶部侍郎李玨曰：「卿有鄭注乎？

translations.literal: When Zhu had first gained favor, the emperor once asked the Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Li Jue, "Do you have Zheng Zhu?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu first won favor, the emperor once asked Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Li Jue, "Do you know Zheng Zhu?

sentences.zh: 亦嘗與之言乎？」

translations.literal: Have you also spoken with him?"
translations.idiomatic: Have you ever spoken with him?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣豈特知其姓名，兼深知其為人。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject—how could he merely know his name? I also know deeply what manner of man he is.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your Majesty, I do not merely know his name—I know the man himself very well.

sentences.zh: 其人奸邪，陛下寵之，恐無益聖德。

translations.literal: That man is treacherous and wicked; if Your Majesty favors him, I fear it will not benefit sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He is treacherous and wicked; if Your Majesty favors him, I fear it will do your sacred virtue no good.

sentences.zh: 臣忝在近密，安敢與此人交通！」

translations.literal: Your subject, dishonored to be near in secret affairs—how would he dare associate with such a person!"
translations.idiomatic: I stand close to Your Majesty in confidence—how would I dare keep company with such a man!"

sentences.zh: 戊寅，貶玨江州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Jue was demoted to prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Jue was demoted to prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 再貶沈柳州司戶。

translations.literal: Shen was demoted again to registrar of Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was demoted again to registrar of Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔以楊承和庇護宋申易，韋元素、王踐言與李宗閔、李德裕中外連結，受其賂遺。

translations.literal: On bingshen, an edict stated that Yang Chenghe had sheltered Song Shenxi, and that Wei Yuansu and Wang Jianyan, together with Li Zongmin and Li Deyu, had linked inner and outer circles and received their bribes.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen an edict declared that Yang Chenghe had shielded Song Shenxi, and that Wei Yuansu and Wang Jianyan, together with Li Zongmin and Li Deyu, had formed factions inside and outside the palace and taken their bribes.

sentences.zh: 承和可驩州安置，元素可像州安置，踐言可恩州安置，令所在錮送。

translations.literal: Chenghe was to be resettled at Huanzhou, Yuansu at Xiangzhou, and Jianyan at Enzhou; orders were issued that wherever they were, they be escorted under guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghe was to be settled at Huanzhou, Yuansu at Xiangzhou, and Jianyan at Enzhou, with orders to escort them under guard wherever found.

sentences.zh: 楊虞卿、李漢、蕭浣為朋黨之首，貶虞卿虔州司戶，漢汾州司馬，浣遂州司馬。

translations.literal: Yang Yuqing, Li Han, and Xiao Huan were heads of the faction; Yuqing was demoted to registrar of Qianzhou, Han to aide of Fenzhou, and Huan to aide of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuqing, Li Han, and Xiao Huan were named ringleaders of the faction; Yuqing was demoted to registrar of Qianzhou, Han to aide of Fenzhou, and Huan to aide of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋遣使追賜承和、元素、踐言死。

translations.literal: Soon envoys were dispatched in pursuit to grant death to Chenghe, Yuansu, and Jianyan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward envoys were sent after them to order their deaths.

sentences.zh: 時崔潭峻已卒，亦剖棺鞭屍。

translations.literal: At that time Cui Tanjun had already died; his coffin too was opened and his corpse flogged.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Tanjun had already died by then, but his coffin was opened and his corpse flogged as well.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以前廬州刺史羅立言為司農少卿。

translations.literal: On jihai, the former prefect of Luzhou Luo Liyan was made Vice Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, former Luzhou prefect Luo Liyan was appointed vice minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 立言贓吏，以賂結鄭注而得之。

translations.literal: Liyan was a corrupt official who obtained the post by bribes connected to Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Liyan was a corrupt official who had bought the post through bribes to Zheng Zhu.

sentences.zh: 鄭注之入翰林也，中書舍人高元裕草制，言以醫藥奉君親，注銜之。

translations.literal: When Zheng Zhu entered the Hanlin Academy, the Secretariat Drafting Gentleman Gao Yuanyu drafted the edict, wording it as serving lord and parents with medicine; Zhu bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Zhu entered the Hanlin Academy, drafting gentleman Gao Yuanyu wrote the appointment edict in terms of serving the throne and one's parents through medicine; Zhu never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 奏元裕嘗出郊送李宗閔，壬寅，貶元裕閬州刺史。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Yuanyu had once gone to the suburbs to see Li Zongmin off; on renyin, Yuanyu was demoted to prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He accused Yuanyu of having once gone into the suburbs to see Li Zongmin off; on renyin Yuanyu was demoted to prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 元裕，士廉之六世孫也。

translations.literal: Yuanyu was the sixth-generation descendant of Shi Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu was a sixth-generation descendant of Shi Lian.

sentences.zh: 時注與李訓所惡朝士，皆指目為二李之黨，貶逐無虛日，班列殆空，廷中恟恟，上亦知之。

translations.literal: At that time the court gentlemen whom Zhu and Li Xun hated were all pointed at and eyed as members of the Two Li faction; demotions and banishments came day after day without pause, the court ranks were nearly empty, and the court was in uproar—the emperor knew it too.
translations.idiomatic: By then every courtier Zhu and Li Xun hated was branded a partisan of the Two Lis; banishments followed one after another until the ranks were nearly bare, the court in an uproar—and the emperor knew it.

sentences.zh: 訓、注恐為人所搖，九月，癸卯朔，勸上下詔：「應與德裕、宗閔親舊及門生故吏，今日以前貶黜之外，餘皆不問。」

translations.literal: Xun and Zhu feared being swayed by others; in the ninth month, on the guimao new moon, they urged the emperor to issue an edict: "Those who should be kin, old friends, students, and former subordinates of Deyu and Zongmin—apart from those already demoted and banished before today, the rest are all not to be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a backlash, Xun and Zhu persuaded the emperor to issue an edict on the guimao new moon of the ninth month: "All who are kin, old friends, students, or former subordinates of Deyu and Zongmin—except those already punished before today—shall be left unmolested."

sentences.zh: 人情稍安。

translations.literal: Public sentiment gradually calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Public anxiety eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵使王涯奏改江淮、嶺南茶法，增其稅。

translations.literal: Wang Ya, Commissioner of Salt and Iron, memorialized to reform the tea laws of the Jiang-Huai and Lingnan regions and increase their taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and Iron Commissioner Wang Ya proposed reforming the tea laws of the Jiang-Huai and Lingnan circuits and raising the tax.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以鳳翔節度使李聽為忠武節度使，代杜悰。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Li Ting, military commissioner of Fengxiang, was made military commissioner of Zhongwu, replacing Du Cong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Fengxiang military commissioner Li Ting was appointed military commissioner of Zhongwu in place of Du Cong.

sentences.zh: 憲宗之崩也，人皆言宦官陳弘志所為。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong died, everyone said it was the work of the eunuch Chen Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong died, everyone said the eunuch Chen Hongzhi had done it.

sentences.zh: 時弘志為山南東道監軍，李訓為上謀召之，至青泥驛，癸亥，封杖殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Hongzhi was army supervisor of the Shannan East Circuit; Li Xun plotted for the emperor to summon him; when he reached Qingni Post, on guihai he was beaten to death under sealed order.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was then army supervisor on the Shannan East circuit; Li Xun arranged for the emperor to summon him, and when he reached Qingni Post, on guihai he was beaten to death under sealed orders.

sentences.zh: 鄭注求為鳳翔節度使，門下侍郎、同平章事李固言不可。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu sought to be military commissioner of Fengxiang; the Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor Li Guyin objected.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu sought the Fengxiang military commission, but Vice Director Li Guyin, associate grand councillor, opposed it.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以固言為山南西道節度使、注為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Guyin was made military commissioner of the Shannan West Circuit and Zhu military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Guyin was sent out as military commissioner of the Shannan West circuit and Zhu as military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 李訓雖因注得進，及勢位俱盛，心頗忌注。

translations.literal: Although Li Xun had advanced through Zhu, once their power and positions were all grand, in his heart he was quite jealous of Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Though Li Xun had risen through Zhu's patronage, once both were at the height of power he grew jealous of him.

sentences.zh: 謀欲中外協勢以誅宦官，故出注於鳳翔。

translations.literal: He plotted to coordinate inner and outer power to execute the eunuchs, and therefore sent Zhu out to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to combine court and provincial force to destroy the eunuchs, and so posted Zhu to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 其實俟既誅宦官，併圖注也。

translations.literal: In truth he waited until after the eunuchs were executed, then would together plot against Zhu as well.
translations.idiomatic: In truth he meant to deal with Zhu once the eunuchs were gone.

sentences.zh: 注欲取名家才望之士為參佐，請禮部員外郎韋溫為副使，溫不可。

translations.literal: Zhu wished to take gentlemen of famous families with talent and reputation as aides; he requested Wei Wen, an assistant in the Ministry of Rites, as deputy commissioner, but Wen refused.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu wanted men of distinguished family and reputation as staff; he asked Vice Director of Rites Wei Wen to serve as his deputy, but Wen declined.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「拒之必為患。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "If you refuse him, it will surely become a trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Some said, "Refuse him and you are asking for trouble."

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「擇禍莫若輕。

translations.literal: Wen said: "In choosing between calamities, none is lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Wen replied, "Of two evils, choose the lesser.

sentences.zh: 拒之止於遠貶，從之有不測之禍。」

translations.literal: Refusing him stops at distant demotion; following him has calamity beyond measure."
translations.idiomatic: Refusal at most means exile far away; compliance brings disaster you cannot foresee."

sentences.zh: 卒辭之。

translations.literal: In the end he declined the post.
translations.idiomatic: He declined in the end.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以右神策中尉、行右衛上將軍、知內侍省事王守澄為左、右神策觀軍容使，兼十二衛統軍。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Wang Shoucheng, Right Commissioner of the Divine Strategy Army, acting General of the Right Guards, Director of Palace Affairs, was made Commandant overseeing the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and Commander-in-Chief of the Twelve Guards.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Wang Shoucheng—right eunuch commissioner of the Divine Strategy army, acting general of the right guards, and head of palace affairs—was named overseer of both Divine Strategy armies and commander-in-chief of the twelve guards.

sentences.zh: 李訓、鄭注為上謀，以虛名尊守澄，實奪之權也。

translations.literal: Li Xun and Zheng Zhu schemed for the emperor: with an empty title they honored Shoucheng, but in truth they stripped away his power.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun and Zheng Zhu persuaded the emperor to promote Shoucheng in name while actually robbing him of power.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以御史中丞兼刑部侍郎舒元輿為刑部侍郎，兵部郎中知制誥、充翰林侍講學士李訓為禮部侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: On jisi, Shu Yuanyu, Censor-in-Chief concurrent Vice Minister of Justice, was made Vice Minister of Justice; Li Xun, Bureau Director in the Ministry of War who drafted edicts and served as Hanlin Lecturer, was made Vice Minister of Rites; both were made Associate Grand Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Justice Shu Yuanyu became Minister of Justice; Li Xun, Bureau Director in War who held drafting duties and lectured in Hanlin, became Minister of Rites; both joined the grand council.

sentences.zh: 仍命訓三二日一入翰林講《易》。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Xun to enter Hanlin every two or three days to lecture on the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was also told to lecture on the Changes in Hanlin every few days.

sentences.zh: 元輿為中丞，凡訓、注所惡者，則為之彈擊，由是得為相。

translations.literal: When Yuanyu was Censor-in-Chief, whenever someone was hated by Xun and Zhu he would impeach them; by this he became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: As censor-in-chief, Yuanyu impeached anyone Xun or Zhu disliked and so won a seat as grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 又上懲李宗閔、李德裕多朋黨，以賈餗及元輿皆孤寒新進，故擢為相，庶其無黨耳。

translations.literal: The emperor also punished Li Zongmin and Li Deyu for factionalism, and because Jia Su and Yuanyu were both obscure newcomers he elevated them to chief ministers, hoping they would be without factions.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise penalized Li Zongmin and Li Deyu for cliques, and raised Jia Su and Yuanyu—both outsiders without patronage—in hopes they would govern without factions.

sentences.zh: 訓起流人，期年致位宰相，天子傾意任之。

translations.literal: Xun rose from exile; within a year he reached grand councillor; the Son of Heaven bent all favor upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had been an exile; within a year he was grand councillor, and the emperor gave him his full trust.

sentences.zh: 訓或在中書，或在翰林，天下事皆決於訓。

translations.literal: Whether Xun was at the Secretariat or in Hanlin, all affairs under Heaven were decided by Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Whether at the Secretariat or in Hanlin, Xun decided every matter of state.

sentences.zh: 而涯輩承順其風旨，惟恐不逮。

translations.literal: Wang Ya and the others followed his intent, fearing only that they could not keep pace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya and his fellows rushed to follow his lead, afraid of falling behind.

sentences.zh: 自中尉、樞密、禁衛諸將，見訓皆震慴，迎拜叩首。

translations.literal: From the eunuch commissioners and directors of the Palace Secretariat down to the generals of the palace guards, those who saw Xun were all shaken with fear and came forward bowing and knocking their heads to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: From eunuch commissioners and secretariat directors to palace guard generals, all trembled before Xun and kowtowed on meeting him.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以刑部郎中兼御史知雜李孝本權知御史中丞。

translations.literal: On renshen, Li Xiaoben, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice concurrent Acting Censor, was made Acting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Li Xiaoben, a bureau director in Justice serving as acting censor, was named acting censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 孝本，宗室之子，依訓、注得進。

translations.literal: Xiaoben was a son of the imperial clan; he advanced by relying on Xun and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoben, a clansman, had risen through Xun's and Zhu's favor.

sentences.zh: 李聽自恃勳舊，不禮於鄭注。

translations.literal: Li Ting relied on his old military merit and showed no courtesy toward Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting, proud of his long service, would not defer to Zheng Zhu.

sentences.zh: 注代聽鎮鳳翔，先遣牙將丹駿至軍中慰勞，誣奏聽在鎮貪虐。

translations.literal: When Zhu replaced Ting as military commissioner of Fengxiang, he first sent his adjutant general Dan Jun to the army to offer condolences, and falsely memorialized that Ting was greedy and cruel in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu took Fengxiang from Ting and sent adjutant Dan Jun ahead to comfort the troops while accusing Ting of greed and cruelty on station.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙亥，以聽為太子太保、分司，復以杜悰為忠武節度使。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yihai, Ting was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with duties in absentia; Du Cong was again made military commissioner of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, yihai: Ting was named grand mentor of the heir and sent into retirement at court; Du Cong returned as Zhongwu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鄭注每自負經濟之略，上問以富人之術，注無以對，乃請榷茶。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu often boasted of his expertise in statecraft; when the emperor asked him the art of enriching the realm, Zhu had nothing to answer and therefore requested a government tea monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu trumpeted his economic genius, but when the emperor asked how to enrich the state he had no reply and proposed a tea monopoly instead.

sentences.zh: 於是以王涯兼榷茶使，涯知不可而不敢違，人甚苦之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Ya was made concurrent Tea Monopoly Commissioner; Ya knew it was wrong but dared not disobey, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya was then put in charge of the tea monopoly; he knew the scheme was ruinous but dared not refuse, and the people bore the cost.

sentences.zh: 鄭注欲收僧尼之譽，固請罷沙汰，從之。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu wished to win the praise of monks and nuns and firmly requested that the purging of the clergy be stopped; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu sought favor among Buddhist clergy and pressed to halt the purge of monks and nuns; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 李訓、鄭注密言於上，請除王守澄。

translations.literal: Li Xun and Zheng Zhu spoke secretly to the emperor, requesting that Wang Shoucheng be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun and Zheng Zhu privately urged the emperor to eliminate Wang Shoucheng.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，遣中使李好古就第賜鴆，殺之，贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the emperor sent the palace messenger Li Haogu to his residence to bestow poisoned wine; he was killed and posthumously made Grand Protector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi a court messenger brought poisoned wine to Shoucheng's home; he died and was posthumously made grand protector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 訓、注本因守澄進，卒謀而殺之，人皆快守澄之受佞而疾訓、注之陰狡，於是元和之逆黨略盡矣。

translations.literal: Xun and Zhu had originally advanced through Shoucheng; in the end they plotted and killed him. Men were all pleased that Shoucheng had received the flatterers' due and detested Xun and Zhu's secret treachery; thus the partisans of the Yuanhe era were largely gone.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Zhu had risen through Shoucheng yet ended by killing him; people rejoiced at Shoucheng's fall to flatterers and loathed Xun and Zhu's deceit—so the Yuanhe faction was nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，鄭注赴鎮。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Zheng Zhu departed for his post.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Zheng Zhu left for Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以東都留守、司徒兼侍中裴度兼中書令，餘如故。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Pei Du, Eastern Capital Intendant, Grand Preceptor concurrent Palace Attendant, was also made Director of the Secretariat; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Pei Du, eastern capital intendant and grand preceptor with palace attendant rank, was also named director of the Secretariat; his other titles stood.

sentences.zh: 李訓所獎拔，率皆狂險之士，然亦時取天下重望認順人心，如裴度、令狐楚、鄭覃皆累朝耆俊，久為當路所軋，置之散地，訓皆引居崇秩。

translations.literal: Those Li Xun promoted and rewarded were mostly reckless and dangerous men; yet he also at times took men of great renown throughout the realm to win people's hearts—such as Pei Du, Linghu Chu, and Zheng Tan, all elders of many reigns, long crushed by those in power and placed in idle posts; Xun all drew them to lofty rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's appointees were usually brash adventurers, but he also placed men of wide esteem—Pei Du, Linghu Chu, Zheng Tan—veterans sidelined for years, to reassure the court.

sentences.zh: 由是士大夫亦有望其真能致太平者，不惟天子惑之也。

translations.literal: Hence the gentry also hoped he might truly bring great peace—not only the emperor was deluded.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars therefore hoped he might restore peace, not the emperor alone.

sentences.zh: 然識者見其橫甚，知將敗矣。

translations.literal: Yet those who understood, seeing how overbearing he was, knew he would soon be ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Observers, noting his arrogance, foresaw his fall.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙午，以大理卿郭行餘為邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingwu, Guo Xingyu, Director of the Court of Judicial Review, was made military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, bingwu: Review Court director Guo Xingyu became Binning military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以河東節度使、同平章事李載義兼侍中。

translations.literal: On guichou, Li Zaiyi, military commissioner of Hedong and associate grand councillor, was also made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Hedong military commissioner and associate grand councillor Li Zaiyi was also named palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以戶部尚書、判度支王璠為河東節度使。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Wang Fan, Minister of Revenue presiding over the budget, was made military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi revenue minister and budget chief Wang Fan became Hedong military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以京兆尹李石為戶部侍郎、判度支；

translations.literal: On wuwu, Li Shi, Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, was made Vice Minister of Revenue presiding over the budget;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Jingzhao governor Li Shi became vice minister of revenue in charge of the budget;

sentences.zh: 以京兆少尹羅立言權知府事。

translations.literal: Luo Liyan, Assistant Metropolitan Governor, was made Acting Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant governor Luo Liyan was left to run the capital prefecture.

sentences.zh: 石，神符之五世孫也。

translations.literal: Shi was the fifth-generation descendant of Li Shenfu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi was a fifth-generation descendant of Li Shenfu.

sentences.zh: 己未，以太府卿韓約為左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Han Yue, Director of the Grand Storehouse, was made General of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei grand storehouse director Han Yue became general of the left Golden Crow guard.

sentences.zh: 始，鄭注與李訓謀，至鎮，選壯士數百，皆持白棓，懷其斧，以為親兵。

translations.literal: At the outset Zheng Zhu and Li Xun had plotted that when Zhu reached his post he would select several hundred stalwart men, each bearing a white club and carrying hatchets in their robes, as personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu and Xun had planned that on reaching Fengxiang Zhu would recruit hundreds of strong men with white staffs and hidden axes as a private guard.

sentences.zh: 是月，戊辰，王守澄葬於滻水，注奏請入護葬事，因以親兵自隨。

translations.literal: That month on wuchen, Wang Shoucheng was buried at Chan River; Zhu memorialized asking to enter and oversee the funeral, taking his private troops with him.
translations.idiomatic: That month, wuchen, at Shoucheng's burial on the Chan, Zhu asked leave to attend the funeral with his armed followers.

sentences.zh: 仍奏令內臣中尉以下盡集滻水送葬，注因闔門，令親兵斧之，使無遺類。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that all eunuchs from the commissioners downward should gather at Chan River for the burial; Zhu then would shut the gate and have his private troops hack them down so that none survived.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed luring every eunuch down to the funeral, then sealing the gates and slaughtering them with his guard.

sentences.zh: 約既定，訓與其黨謀：「如此事成，則注專有其功，不若使行餘、璠以赴鎮為名，多募壯士為部曲，並用金吾、台府吏卒，先期誅宦者，已而並注去之。」

translations.literal: Once the plan was set, Xun and his faction plotted: "If this succeeds, Zhu alone will have the credit; better to have Xingyu and Fan go to their posts in name and recruit many stalwarts as personal followers, and together use Golden Crow and censorate clerks and soldiers to kill the eunuchs first, then afterward get rid of Zhu too."
translations.idiomatic: Xun and his faction plotted, "If this succeeds, Zhu will claim all the credit. Better to have Xingyu, Fan, and the others use departure for their commands as a pretext, recruit brave men as retainers, add Golden Crow and Censorate troops, kill the eunuchs ahead of schedule, and then remove Zhu too."

sentences.zh: 行餘、璠、立言、約及中丞李孝本，皆訓素所厚也，故列置要地，獨與是數人及舒元輿謀之，它人皆莫之知也。

translations.literal: Xingyu, Fan, Liyan, Yue, and Acting Censor-in-Chief Li Xiaoben were all long favored by Xun; therefore they were placed in key posts; only with these men and Shu Yuanyu did he plot; others did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu, Fan, Liyan, Yue, and Li Xiaoben—Xun's trusted men—were stationed strategically; only they and Shu Yuanyu knew the plot.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，上御紫宸殿。

translations.literal: On renxu, the emperor held court in the Zichen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the emperor convened court in Purple Dawn Hall.

sentences.zh: 百官班定，韓約不報平安，奏稱：「左金吾聽事後石榴夜有甘露，臣遞門奏訖。」

translations.literal: When the hundred officials had formed their ranks, Han Yue did not report all secure; he memorialized: "Behind the reception hall of the Left Golden Crow sweet dew appeared on the pomegranate tree at night; I passed through the gate and have finished memorializing."
translations.idiomatic: When the officials were in rank, Han Yue skipped the usual security report and announced, "Last night sweet dew formed on a pomegranate tree behind the Left Golden Crow hall; your servant has already sent the report through the gates."

sentences.zh: 因蹈舞再拜，宰相亦帥百官稱賀。

translations.literal: He then danced and bowed twice; the chief ministers also led the hundred officials in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed twice in ritual joy; the chief ministers led the court in congratulations.

sentences.zh: 訓、元輿勸上親往觀之，以承天貺，上許之。

translations.literal: Xun and Yuanyu urged the emperor to go in person to view it, to receive Heaven's gift; the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Yuanyu persuaded him to see it himself as heaven's blessing; he agreed.

sentences.zh: 百官退，班於含元殿。

translations.literal: The hundred officials withdrew and formed ranks at the Hanyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The officials withdrew to form ranks at Manifest Origin Hall.

sentences.zh: 日加辰，上乘軟輿出紫宸門，升含元殿。

translations.literal: As the day reached the chen hour, the emperor rode a palanquin out the Zichen Gate and ascended the Hanyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-morning, the emperor was carried out through Purple Dawn Gate to Manifest Origin Hall.

sentences.zh: 先命宰相及兩省官詣左仗視之，良久而還。

translations.literal: He first ordered the chief ministers and officials of the two secretariats to go view it at the left review stand; after a long while they returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent chief ministers and secretariat officials to inspect the left review stand; they were gone a long time.

sentences.zh: 訓奏：「臣與眾人驗之，殆非真甘露，未可遽宣佈，恐天下稱賀。」

translations.literal: Xun memorialized: "I examined it with the crowd; it is probably not true sweet dew; it cannot be announced hastily, lest the realm congratulate."
translations.idiomatic: Xun reported that the "dew" looked false and warned against premature celebration.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「豈有是邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How could that be!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "Surely not!"

sentences.zh: 顧左、右中尉仇士良、魚志弘帥諸宦者往視之。

translations.literal: He turned to the Left and Right Commissioners Chou Shiliang and Yu Zhihong to lead the various eunuchs to go view it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent eunuch commissioners Chou Shiliang and Yu Zhihong with the palace staff to verify it.

sentences.zh: 宦者既去，訓遽召郭行餘、王璠曰：「來受敕旨！」

translations.literal: Once the eunuchs had gone, Xun hastily summoned Guo Xingyu and Wang Fan, saying: "Come receive the imperial command!"
