translations.idiomatic: As the eunuchs left, Xun called Xingyu and Fan: "Come for your orders!"

sentences.zh: 璠股慄不敢前，獨行餘拜殿下。

translations.literal: Fan's legs trembled and he did not dare advance; only Xingyu bowed below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Fan shook and hung back; only Xingyu bowed on the steps.

sentences.zh: 時二人部曲數百，皆執兵立丹鳳門外，訓已先使人召之，令人受敕。

translations.literal: At that time several hundred men in their personal retinues all held weapons and stood outside the Vermilion Phoenix Gate; Xun had already sent men ahead to summon them, ordering men to receive the command.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds in their retinues waited armed outside Vermilion Phoenix Gate; Xun had sent orders for them to enter on command.

sentences.zh: 獨東兵入，邠寧兵竟不至。

translations.literal: Only the eastern troops entered; the Binning soldiers never arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hedong troops came in; the Binning force never showed.

sentences.zh: 仇士良等至左仗視甘露，韓約變色流汗。

translations.literal: When Chou Shiliang and the others reached the left review stand to view the sweet dew, Han Yue turned pale and sweated.
translations.idiomatic: At the left review stand, Han Yue went pale and sweaty as Chou Shiliang approached the "dew."

sentences.zh: 士良怪之曰：「將軍何為如是？」

translations.literal: Shiliang, wondering, said: "General, why are you like this?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang asked, "Why do you look so frightened, General?"

sentences.zh: 俄風吹幕起，見執兵者甚眾，又聞兵仗聲，士良等驚駭走出。

translations.literal: Before long the wind blew the curtain up; they saw many holding weapons; they also heard the sound of arms; Shiliang and the others fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Wind lifted the curtain; armed men packed the hall; at the clash of weapons Shiliang and his party bolted.

sentences.zh: 門者欲閉之，士良叱之，關不得上。

translations.literal: The gatekeepers wished to shut the gates; Shiliang shouted at them; the gates could not be closed.
translations.idiomatic: Gatekeepers tried to shut them; Shiliang's shout kept the doors from closing.

sentences.zh: 士良等奔詣上告變。

translations.literal: Shiliang and the others ran to tell the emperor of the mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: They raced to warn the emperor of treason.

sentences.zh: 訓見之，遽呼金吾衛士曰：「來上殿衛乘輿者，人賞錢百緡！」

translations.literal: When Xun saw them, he hastily called out to the Golden Crow guards: "Whoever comes up the hall to protect the palanquin—each man is rewarded one hundred strings of cash!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing them flee, Xun hurriedly called to the Golden Crow guards, "Come up to the hall and guard the imperial carriage, and each man will receive one hundred strings of cash!"

sentences.zh: 宦官曰：「事急矣，請陛下還宮！」

translations.literal: A eunuch said: "Affairs are urgent—Your Majesty must return to the palace!"
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch cried, "Danger! Majesty, back to the palace!"

sentences.zh: 即舉軟輿，迎上扶升輿，決殿後罘罳，疾趨北出。

translations.literal: They immediately raised the palanquin, helped the emperor up into it, cut the rear screens of the hall, and hurried north out.
translations.idiomatic: They lifted the palanquin, broke through the rear screens, and rushed north.

sentences.zh: 訓攀輿呼曰：「臣奏事未竟，陛下不可入宮！」

translations.literal: Xun clung to the palanquin and shouted: "I have not finished memorializing—Your Majesty must not enter the palace!"
translations.idiomatic: Xun grabbed the carriage and shouted, "Your servant has not finished reporting; Your Majesty must not enter the palace!"

sentences.zh: 金吾兵已登殿。

translations.literal: The Golden Crow soldiers had already mounted the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Crow troops were already on the hall steps.

sentences.zh: 羅立言帥京兆邏卒三百餘自東來，李孝本帥御史台從人二百餘自西來，皆登殿縱擊，宦官流血呼冤，死傷者十餘人，乘輿迤邐入宣政門，訓攀輿呼益急，上叱之，宦者郗志榮奮拳毆其胸，偃於地。

translations.literal: Luo Liyan led more than three hundred Jingzhao patrol soldiers from the east; Li Xiaoben led more than two hundred censorate attendants from the west; both mounted the hall and struck freely; eunuchs shouted in blood and grievance; more than ten were killed or wounded; the palanquin wound slowly into the Xuanzheng Gate; Xun clung to the palanquin shouting ever more urgently; the emperor shouted at him; the eunuch Xi Zhirong struck his chest with his fist and he collapsed on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Liyan's three hundred capital patrolmen and Li Xiaoben's two hundred clerks stormed the hall from east and west; eunuchs fell screaming; over ten died; the emperor's carriage inched through Xuanzheng Gate while Xun clung on until Xi Zhirong knocked him down with a blow to the chest.

sentences.zh: 乘輿即入，門隨闔，宦者皆呼萬歲，百官駭散出。

translations.literal: The palanquin entered at once; the gates shut behind them; the eunuchs all cried "Long live the Emperor!"; the hundred officials fled out in fright.
translations.idiomatic: The gates slammed shut behind the emperor as eunuchs shouted long life; officials scattered in panic.

sentences.zh: 訓知事不濟，脫從吏綠衫衣之，走馬而出，揚言於道曰：「我何罪而竄謫！」

translations.literal: Xun knew the affair had failed; he stripped off his green official servant's robe and put it on, mounted a horse and fled, proclaiming along the road: "What crime do I have that I am exiled!"
translations.idiomatic: Realizing defeat, Xun put on a clerk's green robe, rode out, and called along the road, "What crime have I committed that I am being banished!"

sentences.zh: 人不之疑。

translations.literal: People did not doubt him.
translations.idiomatic: No one stopped him.

sentences.zh: 王涯、賈餗、舒元輿還中書，相謂曰：「上且開延英，召吾屬議之。」

translations.literal: Wang Ya, Jia Su, and Shu Yuanyu returned to the Secretariat and said to one another: "The emperor will presently open Extended Grace and summon us to discuss it."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya, Jia Su, and Shu Yuanyu returned to the Secretariat and said to one another, "His Majesty will soon open Extended Grace Hall and summon us to discuss this."

sentences.zh: 兩省官詣宰相請其故，皆曰：「不知何事，諸公各自便！」

translations.literal: Officials of the two secretariats went to the chief ministers to ask the reason; they all said: "We do not know what affair it is—gentlemen, each take your ease!"
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the two departments went to the chief ministers and asked what had happened; they all said, "We do not know what this is. Gentlemen, each of you should go as you please!"

sentences.zh: 士良等知上豫其謀，怨憤，出不遜語，上慚懼不復言。

translations.literal: Shiliang and the others knew the emperor had foreknown their plot and were resentful and furious; they spoke insolent words; the emperor was ashamed and afraid and spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang knew the emperor had colluded with the plotters; enraged, he insulted him until the emperor shrank into silence.

sentences.zh: 士良等命左、右神策副使劉泰倫、魏仲卿等各帥禁兵五百人，露刃出閣門討賊。

translations.literal: Shiliang and the others ordered the Left and Right Divine Strategy Deputy Commandants Liu Tailun and Wei Zhongqing each to lead five hundred palace soldiers with bare blades out the Ge Gate to pursue the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang sent deputy commanders Liu Tailun and Wei Zhongqing, each with five hundred guards and drawn swords, out Ge Gate to hunt the rebels.

sentences.zh: 王涯等將會食，吏白：「有兵自內出，逢人輒殺！」

translations.literal: Wang Ya and the others were about to take their meal when clerks reported: "Soldiers have come out from within—whoever they meet they kill!"
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Ya and the others were about to eat together, a clerk reported, "Troops are coming out from inside the palace, killing everyone they meet!"

sentences.zh: 涯等狼狽步走，兩省及金吾吏卒千餘人填門爭出。

translations.literal: Ya and the others fled in disheveled haste on foot; more than a thousand men of the two secretariats and Golden Crow clerks and soldiers clogged the gate struggling to get out.
translations.idiomatic: They ran; a thousand secretariat and Golden Crow staff jammed the exit.

sentences.zh: 門尋闔，其不得出者六百餘人皆死。

translations.literal: Before long the gate was shut; those who could not get out—more than six hundred—were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: The gate closed; six hundred trapped inside died.

sentences.zh: 士良等分兵閉宮門，索諸司，討賊黨。

translations.literal: Shiliang and the others divided troops to shut the palace gates, searched the various offices, and pursued the rebel faction.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang sealed the palace gates and scoured ministries for conspirators.

sentences.zh: 諸司吏卒及民酤販在中者皆死，死者又千餘人，橫屍流血，狼籍塗地，諸司印及圖籍、帷幕、器皿俱盡。

translations.literal: Clerks and soldiers of the various offices and merchants selling wine within were all killed; another thousand-odd died; corpses lay across the ground in blood; seals and registers, curtains and vessels of the offices were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks, runners, and shopkeepers caught inside were slaughtered—another thousand dead; blood soaked the floors; office seals, archives, hangings, and furnishings were ruined.

sentences.zh: 又遣騎各千餘出城追亡者，又遣兵大索城中。

translations.literal: They also sent cavalry, each a thousand strong, out of the city to pursue fugitives, and sent troops to search the city broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry thousands strong rode out to chase fugitives while troops combed the capital.

sentences.zh: 舒元輿易服單騎出安化門，禁兵追擒之。

translations.literal: Shu Yuanyu changed clothes and rode out alone through the Anhua Gate; palace soldiers pursued and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu swapped clothes and fled alone through Anhua Gate; guards caught him.

sentences.zh: 王涯徒步至永昌裡茶肆，禁兵擒入左軍。

translations.literal: Wang Ya went on foot to a teahouse in Yongchang Lane; palace soldiers seized him and took him into the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya walked to a teahouse in Yongchang Lane; guards dragged him to the Left Army prison.

sentences.zh: 涯時年七十餘，被以桎梏，掠治不勝苦，自誣服，稱與李訓謀行大逆，尊立鄭注。

translations.literal: Ya was then more than seventy years old; they put shackles on him; under torture he could not endure the suffering and falsely confessed, saying he had plotted with Li Xun to commit great treason and elevate Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Over seventy, he was shackled and tortured until he confessed to plotting with Li Xun to make Zhu emperor.

sentences.zh: 王璠歸長興坊私第，閉門，以其兵自防。

translations.literal: Wang Fan returned to his private residence in Changxing Ward, shut the door, and used his troops to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan barricaded his home in Changxing Ward with his own troops.

sentences.zh: 神策將至門，呼曰：「王涯等謀反，欲起尚書為相，魚護軍令致意！」

translations.literal: When Divine Strategy troops reached the gate they shouted: "Wang Ya and the others have rebelled and wish to make you chief minister—Army Protector Yu sends his regards!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Shence troops reached the gate, they shouted, "Wang Ya and the others have rebelled and want to make the minister chief minister; Protector Yu sends his respects!"

sentences.zh: 璠喜，出見之。

translations.literal: Fan was pleased and came out to see them.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Fan came out to meet them.

sentences.zh: 將趨賀再三，璠知見紿，涕泣而行，至左軍，見王涯曰：「二十兄自反，胡為見引？」

translations.literal: The generals urged him repeatedly to offer congratulations; Fan knew he had been deceived, wept as he walked, and when he reached the Left Army and saw Wang Ya said: "Elder Brother Twenty rebelled on your own—why drag me in?"
translations.idiomatic: Urged to congratulate the new order, Fan realized the trick, wept all the way to the Left Army, and asked Wang Ya, "Brother Twenty rebelled alone—why implicate me?"

sentences.zh: 涯曰：「五弟昔為京兆尹，不漏言於王守澄，豈有今日邪！」

translations.literal: Ya said: "Younger Brother Five, in the past when you were Metropolitan Governor you did not leak word to Wang Shoucheng—would there be today?"
translations.idiomatic: Ya replied, "When you were capital governor you never tipped Shoucheng—so we are here."

sentences.zh: 璠俯首不言。

translations.literal: Fan bowed his head and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Fan only hung his head in silence.

sentences.zh: 又收羅立言於太平裡，及涯等親屬奴婢，皆入兩軍系之。

translations.literal: They also seized Luo Liyan in Taiping Lane, and Ya's and the others' kinfolk and slaves and maidservants—all were put in the two armies and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Liyan was taken in Taiping Lane; kinsmen and servants of the chief plotters were jailed in both army compounds.

sentences.zh: 戶部員外郎李元皋，訓之再從弟也，訓實與之無恩，亦執而殺之。

translations.literal: Li Yuangao, an assistant in the Ministry of Revenue, was Xun's second cousin once removed; Xun in truth had no kindness toward him, yet they seized and killed him too.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuangao, a revenue aide and Xun's distant cousin, was killed though Xun had never favored him.

sentences.zh: 故嶺南節度使胡證，家巨富，禁兵利其財，托以搜賈餗入其家，執其子殷，殺之。

translations.literal: The former military commissioner of Lingnan Hu Zheng's household was enormously rich; palace soldiers coveted his wealth and used the pretext of searching for Jia Su to enter his house; they seized his son Yin and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guards looted the vast estate of former Lingnan commissioner Hu Zheng, using a search for Jia Su as cover, and murdered his son Yin.

sentences.zh: 又入左常侍羅讓、詹事渾金歲、翰林學士黎埴等家，掠其貲財，掃地無遺。

translations.literal: They also entered the houses of Left Regular Attendant Luo Rang, Household Administration Director Hun Jinnsui, and Hanlin Academician Li Zhi, plundering their wealth until nothing remained.
translations.idiomatic: They raided the homes of Luo Rang, Hun Jinnsui, and Li Zhi and stripped them bare.

sentences.zh: 金歲，瑊之子也，坊市惡少年因之報私仇，殺人，剽掠百貨。

translations.literal: Jinnsui was the son of Hun Zhen; the bad youths of the wards used the occasion to settle private scores, killing people and looting goods.
translations.idiomatic: Jinnsui was Hun Zhen's son; street toughs joined in to settle grudges and plunder shops.

sentences.zh: 互相攻劫，塵埃蔽天。

translations.literal: They attacked and robbed one another; dust obscured the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Mobs robbed one another until dust blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，百官入朝，日出，始開建福門，惟聽以從者一人自隨，禁兵露刃夾道。

translations.literal: On guihai the hundred officials entered court; the sun had risen before the Jianfu Gate was opened; they were allowed only one attendant each; palace soldiers with bare blades lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: Guihai: officials came to court; Jianfu Gate opened only after sunrise; each was allowed one follower; armed guards lined the route.

sentences.zh: 至宣政門，尚未開。

translations.literal: When they reached the Xuanzheng Gate it had still not opened.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanzheng Gate they waited in vain for entry.

sentences.zh: 時無宰相御史知班，百官無復班列。

translations.literal: At that time there was no chief minister to order the ranks for the censorate; the hundred officials no longer formed their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: With no grand councillor or duty censor to form ranks, the procession collapsed.

sentences.zh: 上御紫宸殿，問：「宰相何為不來？」

translations.literal: The emperor held court in the Zichen Hall and asked: "Why have the chief ministers not come?"
translations.idiomatic: In Purple Dawn Hall the emperor asked, "Why have the chief ministers not come?"

sentences.zh: 仇士良曰：「王涯等謀反繫獄。」

translations.literal: Chou Shiliang said: "Wang Ya and the others plotted rebellion and are imprisoned."
translations.idiomatic: Chou Shiliang answered, "Wang Ya and his fellows are jailed for treason."

sentences.zh: 因以涯手狀呈上，召左僕射令狐楚、右僕射鄭覃等升殿示之。

translations.literal: He thereupon presented Ya's handwritten deposition to the emperor, summoned the Left Vice Director Linghu Chu, Right Vice Director Zheng Tan, and others to ascend the hall and show it to them.
translations.idiomatic: He then showed the emperor Wang Ya's own handwriting, and summoned Linghu Chu, Zheng Tan, and others to the hall to view it.

sentences.zh: 上悲憤不自勝，謂楚等曰：「是涯手書乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor, grief and rage beyond bearing, said to Chu and the others: "Is this in Ya's own hand?"
translations.idiomatic: Overcome with grief and rage, the emperor asked Chu and the rest, "Is this Wang Ya's own writing?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「是也！」

translations.literal: They replied: "It is!"
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "It is."

sentences.zh: 「誠如此，罪不容誅！」

translations.literal: If it is truly so, his crime admits no punishment short of death!"
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, he deserves death beyond measure!"

sentences.zh: 因命楚、覃留宿中書，參決機務。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Chu and Tan to lodge overnight at the Secretariat and participate in deciding urgent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Chu and Tan to stay overnight at the Secretariat to handle state business.

sentences.zh: 使楚草制宣告中外。

translations.literal: He had Chu draft an edict to proclaim the matter within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Chu was told to draft a proclamation for court and country.

sentences.zh: 楚敘王涯、賈餗反事浮泛，仇士良等不悅，由是不得為相。

translations.literal: Chu's account of Wang Ya and Jia Su's rebellion was vague and superficial; Chou Shiliang and the others were displeased, and for this reason he was not made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's draft treated the Wang Ya–Jia Su plot too lightly; Chou Shiliang and his party were displeased, and Chu was never made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 時坊市剽掠者猶未止，命左、右神策將楊鎮、靳遂良等各將五百人分屯通衢，擊鼓以警之，斬十餘人，然後定。

translations.literal: At that time the plunderers in the wards and markets had still not ceased; he ordered the Left and Right Shence generals Yang Zhen and Jin Suiliang, each leading five hundred men, to station separately along the main thoroughfares, beat drums to warn them, and behead more than ten—only then was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: Looting in the markets continued; Yang Zhen and Jin Suiliang were sent with five hundred guards each to hold the main roads, drum warnings, and execute a dozen ringleaders before order returned.

sentences.zh: 賈餗變服潛民間經宿，自知無所逃，素服乘驢詣興安門，自言：「我宰相賈餗也，為奸人所污，可送我詣兩軍！」

translations.literal: Jia Su changed his clothes and hid among the people for a night; knowing he could not escape, in plain dress he rode a donkey to the Xing'an Gate and said himself: "I am the chief minister Jia Su; wicked men have defiled me—take me to the two armies!"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Su disguised himself and hid overnight; seeing no escape, he came to Xing'an Gate in plain clothes on a donkey, saying, "I am Chief Minister Jia Su, slandered by villains—deliver me to the two armies!"

sentences.zh: 門者執送西軍。

translations.literal: The gate guards seized him and sent him to the Western Army.
translations.idiomatic: Gate guards seized him and handed him to the Western Army.

sentences.zh: 李孝本改衣綠，猶服金帶，以帽鄣面，單騎奔鳳翔，至咸陽西，追擒之。

translations.literal: Li Xiaoben changed to green dress but still wore a gold belt; using his hat to cover his face, he rode alone toward Fengxiang; west of Xianyang he was pursued and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoben swapped to green robes but kept his gold belt, masked his face with his hat, and fled alone toward Fengxiang; he was caught west of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以右僕射鄭覃同平章事。

translations.literal: On jiazi he appointed Right Vice Director Zheng Tan Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazi: Zheng Tan, Right Vice Director, was made Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 李訓素與終南僧宗密善，往投之。

translations.literal: Li Xun had long been on good terms with the Zhongnan monk Zongmi and went to seek refuge with him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, who had long been close to the Zhongnan monk Zongmi, fled to him.

sentences.zh: 宗密欲剃其發而匿之，其徒不可。

translations.literal: Zongmi wished to shave his head and hide him; his disciples would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmi wanted to tonsure him and hide him, but his disciples refused.

sentences.zh: 訓出山，將奔鳳翔，為盩厔鎮遏使宋楚所擒，械送京師。

translations.literal: Xun left the mountain, was about to flee to Fengxiang, and was seized by the Zhouzhi suppression commissioner Song Chu, sent to the capital in cangues.
translations.idiomatic: Xun left the hills for Fengxiang, was captured by Zhouzhi commissioner Song Chu, and sent to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 至昆明池，訓恐至軍中更受酷辱，謂送者曰：「得我者則富貴矣！

translations.literal: At Kunming Pool, Xun feared that on reaching the armies he would suffer further cruel humiliation and said to his escorts: "Whoever gets me will be rich and noble!
translations.idiomatic: At Kunming Pool, fearing worse torture in camp, Xun told his escorts, "Whoever takes me will grow rich!

sentences.zh: 聞禁兵所在搜捕，汝必為所奪，不若取我首送之！」

translations.literal: I hear the palace troops are searching everywhere—you will surely be robbed of me; better take my head and deliver that!"
translations.idiomatic: Palace troops are hunting everywhere—you will lose me to them. Better cut off my head and bring that!"

sentences.zh: 送者從之，斬其首以來。

translations.literal: The escorts followed this; they cut off his head and brought it.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed, beheaded him, and carried the head in.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以戶部侍郎、判度支李石同平章事，仍判度支。

translations.literal: On yichou he appointed Ministry of Revenue Vice Minister and acting fiscal commissioner Li Shi Associate Chief Minister, still acting over fiscal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yichou: Li Shi, Revenue Vice Minister and acting fiscal chief, was made Associate Chief Minister and kept fiscal duty.

sentences.zh: 前河東節度使李載義復舊任。

translations.literal: The former Hedong military commissioner Li Zaiyi was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Former Hedong commissioner Li Zaiyi was reappointed.

sentences.zh: 左神策出兵三百人，以李訓首引王涯、王璠、羅立言、郭行餘；

translations.literal: The Left Shence Army sent out three hundred men, with Li Xun's head leading Wang Ya, Wang Fan, Luo Liyan, and Guo Xingyu;
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred Left Shence troops paraded Li Xun's head before Wang Ya, Wang Fan, Luo Liyan, and Guo Xingyu;

sentences.zh: 右神策出兵三百人，擁賈餗、舒元輿、李孝本獻於廟社，徇於兩市。

translations.literal: the Right Shence Army sent out three hundred men, escorting Jia Su, Shu Yuanyu, and Li Xiaoben to present them at the ancestral temples and altars, and displaying them through the two markets.
translations.idiomatic: three hundred Right Shence troops escorted Jia Su, Shu Yuanyu, and Li Xiaoben to the temple altars and through both markets.

sentences.zh: 命百官臨視，腰斬於獨柳之下，梟其首於興安門外。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to witness in person; they were cut at the waist below the Solitary Willow, and their heads were exposed outside the Xing'an Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were ordered to watch as they were cut in two at Solitary Willow and their heads hung outside Xing'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 親屬無問親疏皆死，孩稚無遺，妻女不死者沒為官婢。

translations.literal: Kinsmen without distinction of closeness or distance were all put to death; not even infants were spared; wives and daughters who were not killed were confiscated as government slave-girls.
translations.idiomatic: Kin of every degree were executed, infants included; surviving wives and daughters were taken as government bondwomen.

sentences.zh: 百姓觀者怨王涯榷茶，或詬詈，或投礫擊之。

translations.literal: Among the common people watching, some resented Wang Ya's tea monopoly—some cursed and reviled, some threw stones and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: Spectators, bitter over Wang Ya's tea monopoly, cursed them or pelted them with stones.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：「論者皆謂涯、餗有文學名聲，初不知訓、注之謀，橫罹覆族之禍，憤歎其冤。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang remarks: "Critics all say that Ya and Su had literary fame and reputation, at first did not know Xun and Zhu's plot, and suffered the calamity of exterminated clans by mischance—they lament their injustice in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: "Some say Wang Ya and Jia Su were men of letters who never knew Li Xun and Zheng Zhu's plot and were unjustly wiped out—pity moves them.

sentences.zh: 臣獨以為不然。

translations.literal: Your subject alone holds that this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: I do not agree.

sentences.zh: 夫顛危不扶，焉用彼相！

translations.literal: When the state totters and you do not support it, of what use is such a minister!
translations.idiomatic: If you will not steady a tottering state, what good is that minister?

sentences.zh: 涯、餗安高位，飽重祿；

translations.literal: Ya and Su held lofty posts and were sated with heavy salaries;
translations.idiomatic: Ya and Su held the highest offices and drew heavy salaries;

sentences.zh: 訓、注小人，窮奸究險，力取將相。

translations.literal: Xun and Zhu were petty men who exhausted treachery and pursued villainy to the limit, striving by force to seize the posts of general and chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Zhu were base schemers who stopped at nothing to seize power;

sentences.zh: 涯、餗與之比肩，不以為恥；

translations.literal: Ya and Su stood shoulder to shoulder with them and did not take it as shame;
translations.idiomatic: Ya and Su stood with them without shame;

sentences.zh: 國家危殆，不以為憂。

translations.literal: the state in peril—they did not take it as worry.
translations.idiomatic: they watched the realm in peril without concern.

sentences.zh: 偷合苟容，日復一日，自謂得保身之良策，莫我如也。

translations.literal: Stealing union and seeking easy acceptance day after day, they called it in themselves the fine strategy for preserving body and life—none their equal.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day they clung to office, calling cowardice the sure way to save their skins.

sentences.zh: 若使人人如此而無禍，則奸臣孰不願之哉！

translations.literal: If everyone could be thus without calamity, then which treacherous minister would not wish it!
translations.idiomatic: If every schemer could do the same without ruin, who would not?

sentences.zh: 一旦禍生不虞，足折刑剭，蓋天誅之也，士良安能族之哉！

translations.literal: Once calamity arose unforeseen, feet broken and punishments applied—it was Heaven's execution; how could Shiliang alone have exterminated their clans!
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck, their broken bodies and harsh punishments were Heaven's judgment—Chou Shiliang did not invent their fate.

sentences.zh: 王涯有再從弟沐，家於江南，老且貧。

translations.literal: Wang Ya had a second cousin once removed named Mu, who lived in the south of the Yangtze, old and poor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya's second cousin once removed, Mu, lived in the south, old and poor.

sentences.zh: 聞涯為相，跨驢詣之，欲求一簿、尉。

translations.literal: Hearing that Ya had become chief minister, he rode a donkey to visit him, wishing to obtain a registry or constable post.
translations.idiomatic: When Ya became chief minister, Mu rode a donkey to Chang'an seeking a minor clerkship.

sentences.zh: 留長安二歲餘，始得一見，涯待之殊落莫。

translations.literal: He stayed in Chang'an more than two years before he obtained one audience; Ya treated him extremely coldly.
translations.idiomatic: He waited over two years for one audience; Ya treated him coldly.

sentences.zh: 久之，沐因嬖奴以道所欲，涯許以微官，自是旦夕造涯之門以俟命；

translations.literal: After a long time, Mu through a favorite slave conveyed what he wanted; Ya promised him a minor office, and from then on morning and evening he came to Ya's gate awaiting orders;
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Mu asked a favorite slave to plead; Ya promised a petty post, and Mu haunted his gate morning and night;

sentences.zh: 及涯家被收，沐適在其第，與涯俱腰斬。

translations.literal: when Ya's household was seized, Mu happened to be in his residence and was cut at the waist together with Ya.
translations.idiomatic: when Ya's house was raided, Mu was inside and was cut in two with him.

sentences.zh: 舒元輿有族子守謙，願而敏，元輿愛之，從元輿者十年，一旦忽以非罪怒之，日加譴責，奴婢亦薄之。

translations.literal: Shu Yuanyu had a clansman named Shouqian, handsome and quick-witted; Yuanyu loved him and had kept him for ten years, when suddenly for no crime he grew angry with him and daily increased reproof; the slaves and maidservants also treated him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Yuanyu's clansman Shouqian, clever and favored for ten years, was suddenly and groundlessly berated daily; even servants slighted him.

sentences.zh: 守謙不自安，求歸江南，元輿亦不留，守謙悲歎而去。

translations.literal: Shouqian felt ill at ease, asked to return to the south of the Yangtze; Yuanyu also did not detain him, and Shouqian left in grief and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Shouqian asked to return south; Yuanyu let him go, and he left in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 夕，至昭應，聞元輿收族，守謙獨免。」

translations.literal: That evening he reached Zhaoying; hearing that Yuanyu's clan had been seized and exterminated, Shouqian alone escaped."
translations.idiomatic: That night at Zhaoying he learned Yuanyu's clan was destroyed; Shouqian alone was spared."

sentences.zh: 是日，以令狐楚為鹽鐵轉運使，左散騎常侍張仲方權知京兆尹。

translations.literal: That day Linghu Chu was made salt and iron transport commissioner, and Left Regular Attendant Zhang Zhongfang was appointed acting metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: That day Linghu Chu became salt-and-iron transport commissioner; Zhang Zhongfang, Left Regular Attendant, acted as Jingzhao magistrate.

sentences.zh: 時數日之間，殺生除拜，皆決於兩中尉，上不豫知。

translations.literal: At that time, within a few days, killing, sparing life, and appointments and dismissals were all decided by the two chief eunuchs; the emperor was not beforehand informed.
translations.idiomatic: Within days, executions, pardons, and appointments were settled by the two chief eunuchs without the emperor's foreknowledge.

sentences.zh: 初，王守澄惡官者田全操、劉行深、周元稹、薛士幹、似先義逸、劉英□等，李訓、鄭注因之遣分詣鹽州、靈武、涇原、夏州、振武、鳳翔巡邊，命翰林學士顧師邕為詔書賜六道，使殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Shoucheng hated the eunuchs Tian Quancao, Liu Xingshen, Zhou Yuanzhen, Xue Shigan, Sixian Yiyi, Liu Yingyi, and others; Li Xun and Zheng Zhu used this to send them separately to patrol the borders at Yanzhou, Lingwu, Jingyuan, Xiazhou, Zhenwu, and Fengxiang, ordering Hanlin Academician Gu Shiyong to draft edicts for the six circuits to bestow, commanding them to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Shoucheng had hated eunuchs including Tian Quancao, Liu Xingshen, Zhou Yuanzhen, Xue Shigan, Sixian Yiyi, and Liu Yingyi; Xun and Zhu sent them on border tours to six posts with edicts from Gu Shiyong ordering their deaths.

sentences.zh: 會訓敗，六道得詔，皆廢不行。

translations.literal: When Xun was defeated, the six circuits received the edicts but all discarded them and did not carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun fell, all six circuits received the orders but set them aside.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以師邕為矯詔，下御史獄。

translations.literal: On bingyin Gu Shiyong was charged with forging edicts and sent down to the censorate prison.
translations.idiomatic: Bingyin: Gu Shiyong was jailed for forging edicts.

sentences.zh: 先是，鄭注將親兵五百，已發鳳翔，至扶風。

translations.literal: Before this, Zheng Zhu was about to lead five hundred personal troops, already sent out from Fengxiang, and had reached Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu had already marched five hundred personal troops from Fengxiang as far as Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 扶風令韓遼知其謀，不供具，攜印及吏卒奔武功。

translations.literal: The Fufeng magistrate Han Liao knew their plot and did not supply provisions; he took his seal and clerks and soldiers and fled to Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Fufeng magistrate Han Liao, knowing the plot, refused supplies and fled to Wugong with his seal and staff.

sentences.zh: 注知訓已敗，復還鳳翔。

translations.literal: Zhu, learning that Xun had been defeated, returned again to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Xun had failed, Zhu turned back to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 仇士良等使人繼密敕授鳳翔監軍張仲清令取注，仲清惶惑，不知所為。

translations.literal: Chou Shiliang and the others sent men with successive secret edicts to Fengxiang military supervisor Zhang Zhongqing ordering him to seize Zhu; Zhongqing was fearful and confused, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Chou Shiliang sent secret orders to Fengxiang supervisor Zhang Zhongqing to seize Zhu; Zhongqing was paralyzed.

sentences.zh: 押牙李叔說仲清曰：「叔和為公以好召注，屏其從兵，於坐取之，事立定矣！」

translations.literal: Yayasi Li Shuhuo said to Zhongqing: "Shuhuo will for you summon Zhu with friendly intent, screen off his followers, and take him in his seat—the affair will be settled at once!"
translations.idiomatic: Yayasi Li Shuhuo told Zhongqing, "I will lure Zhu in, separate his guards, and seize him at table—the thing is done in a stroke!"

sentences.zh: 仲清從之，伏甲以待注。

translations.literal: Zhongqing followed this; he hid armed men awaiting Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing agreed and set an ambush.

sentences.zh: 注恃其兵衛，遂詣仲清。

translations.literal: Zhu, relying on his armed guard, then went to visit Zhongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting his escort, Zhu came to Zhongqing.

sentences.zh: 叔和稍引其從兵，享之於外，注獨與數人入。

translations.literal: Shuhuo gradually drew off his followers and entertained them outside; Zhu entered alone with only a few men.
translations.idiomatic: Shuhuo drew the guards off to an outer feast; Zhu entered with only a few men.

sentences.zh: 既啜茶，叔和抽刀斬注，因閉外門，悉誅其親兵。

translations.literal: After they had sipped tea, Shuhuo drew his blade and cut down Zhu; he then closed the outer gate and put to death all his personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: After tea, Shuhuo struck off Zhu's head, shut the gate, and slaughtered his troops.

sentences.zh: 乃出密赦，宣示將士，遂滅注家，並殺副使錢可復、節度判官盧簡能、觀察判官蕭傑、掌書記盧弘茂等及其枝黨，死者千餘人。

translations.literal: He then produced the secret edict, proclaimed it to the officers and soldiers, and thereupon exterminated Zhu's household, and also killed deputy commissioner Qian Kefu, circuit judge Lu Jianneng, surveillance judge Xiao Jie, secretariat recorder Lu Hongmao, and others with their branches and partisans—more than a thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: He read the secret edict to the troops, destroyed Zhu's house, and killed deputy Qian Kefu, judge Lu Jianneng, surveillance judge Xiao Jie, recorder Lu Hongmao, and over a thousand associates.

sentences.zh: 可復，徽之子；

translations.literal: Kefu was the son of Qian Hui;
translations.idiomatic: Kefu was Qian Hui's son;

sentences.zh: 簡能，綸之子；

translations.literal: Jianneng was the son of Lu Lun;
translations.idiomatic: Jianneng was Lu Lun's son;

sentences.zh: 人桀，俛之弟也。

translations.literal: Xiao Jie was the younger brother of Yuan Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jie was Yuan Fu's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 朝廷未知注死，丁卯，詔削奪注官爵，令鄰道案兵觀變。

translations.literal: The court did not yet know Zhu was dead; on dingmao it issued an edict stripping Zhu of office and rank and ordering neighboring circuits to mass troops and watch developments.
translations.idiomatic: The court still did not know Zhu was dead; dingmao: he was stripped of rank and neighboring circuits told to hold troops ready.

sentences.zh: 以左神策大將軍陳君弈為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: The Left Shence Grand General Chen Junyi was made military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Junyi, Left Shence Grand General, was made Fengxiang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 戊辰夜，張仲清遣李叔和等以注首入獻，梟於興安門，人情稍安，京師諸軍始各還營。

translations.literal: At night on wuchen Zhang Zhongqing sent Li Shuhuo and others to enter the capital with Zhu's head; it was exposed at the Xing'an Gate; popular feeling gradually settled, and the capital armies at last each returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchen night: Zhu's head reached the capital and was hung at Xing'an Gate; troops returned to camp and the city calmed.

sentences.zh: 詔將士討賊有功及娖隊者，官爵賜賚各有差。

translations.literal: An edict: officers and soldiers who had merit in suppressing the rebels and the ornamental guard units—ranks, titles, and gifts were each graded.
translations.idiomatic: Merit in suppressing the rebels was rewarded with graded ranks, titles, and gifts.

sentences.zh: 右神策軍獲韓約於崇義坊，己巳，斬之。

translations.literal: The Right Shence Army captured Han Yue in Chongyi Lane; on jisi he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Shence took Han Yue in Chongyi Lane; jisi: he was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 仇士良等各進階遷官有差。

translations.literal: Chou Shiliang and the others each advanced in rank and were promoted with differing grades.
translations.idiomatic: Chou Shiliang and his party were promoted in turn.

sentences.zh: 自是天下事皆決於北司，宰相行文書而已。

translations.literal: From this time forward all affairs under Heaven were decided by the Northern Office; the chief ministers merely issued documents.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Northern Office ruled the empire; chief ministers only issued paperwork.

sentences.zh: 宦官氣益盛，迫脅天子，下視宰相，陵暴朝士如草芥。

translations.literal: The eunuchs' arrogance grew daily; they coerced the Son of Heaven, looked down on the chief ministers, and bullied court gentlemen like grass.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs grew bolder, coerced the emperor, looked down on ministers, and trampled officials like weeds.

sentences.zh: 每延英議事，士良等動引訓、注折宰相。

translations.literal: Whenever they met in Yanying to discuss affairs, Shiliang and the others would bring up Xun and Zhu to bend the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanying sessions they constantly invoked Xun and Zhu to humble the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃、李石曰：「訓、注誠為亂首，但不知訓、注始因何人得進？」

translations.literal: Zheng Tan and Li Shi said: "Xun and Zhu were indeed the ringleaders of rebellion—but do you not know through whom Xun and Zhu first gained advancement?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan and Li Shi said, "Xun and Zhu were rebels—but who first advanced them?"

sentences.zh: 宦者稍屈，縉紳賴之。

translations.literal: The eunuchs slightly yielded; the gentry relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs flinched; the court gentry took heart.

sentences.zh: 時中書惟有空垣破屋，百物皆闕。

translations.literal: At that time in the Secretariat there were only empty walls and ruined houses; a hundred things were lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat held only broken walls; it lacked everything.

sentences.zh: 江西、湖南獻衣糧百二十分，充宰相召募從人。

translations.literal: Jiangxi and Hunan presented one hundred and twenty portions of clothing and grain to supply the chief ministers' recruiting of followers.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi and Hunan sent one hundred and twenty sets of clothing and grain to fund ministers' retainers.

sentences.zh: 辛未，李石上言：「宰相若忠正無邪，神靈所祐，縱遇盜賊，亦不能傷。

translations.literal: On xinwei Li Shi submitted: "If the chief minister is loyal and upright without deviousness, spirits will protect him; even if he meets bandits, they cannot harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Xinwei: Li Shi said, "An upright minister is guarded by spirits; bandits cannot harm him.

sentences.zh: 若內懷奸罔，雖兵衛甚設，鬼得而誅之。

translations.literal: If within he harbors treachery and deceit, though military guards be set thick, how can ghosts obtain and execute him?
translations.idiomatic: But a treacherous heart cannot be saved by guards—Heaven itself will strike him down.

sentences.zh: 臣願竭赤心以報國，止循故事，以金吾卒導從足矣。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to exhaust a loyal heart to repay the state, only following precedent—using Golden Guard soldiers as escort is sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: I will serve with a loyal heart and ask only the usual Golden Guard escort.

sentences.zh: 其兩道所獻衣糧，並乞停寢。」

translations.literal: The clothing and grain presented by the two circuits—your subject asks that all be halted and set aside."
translations.idiomatic: Please halt the gifts from both circuits."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬申朔，顧師邕流儋州，至商山，賜死。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on the ren-shen new moon, Gu Shiyong was banished to Danzhou; at Shangshan he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, ren-shen new moon: Gu Shiyong was exiled to Danzhou and ordered to die at Shangshan.

sentences.zh: 榷茶使令狐楚奏罷榷茶，從之。

translations.literal: The tea monopoly commissioner Linghu Chu memorialized to abolish the tea monopoly; this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Tea monopoly commissioner Linghu Chu petitioned to end the monopoly; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 度支奏籍鄭注家貲，得絹百餘萬匹，他物稱是。

translations.literal: The fiscal office memorialized registering Zheng Zhu's household assets, obtaining more than a million bolts of silk and other goods in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: The fiscal office inventoried Zhu's estate at over a million bolts of silk and comparable goods.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，上問宰相：「坊市安未？」

translations.literal: On gengchen the emperor asked the chief ministers: "Are the wards and markets settled yet?"
translations.idiomatic: Gengchen: the emperor asked the chief ministers, "Are the wards and markets calm yet?"

sentences.zh: 李石對曰：「漸安。

translations.literal: Li Shi replied: "They are gradually settling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi replied, "They are gradually calming.

sentences.zh: 然比日寒冽特甚，蓋刑殺太過所致。」

translations.literal: Yet these days the cold has been exceptionally severe—probably because executions have been excessive."
translations.idiomatic: But the cold in recent days has been especially fierce; it is probably caused by excessive executions."

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「罪人周親前已皆死，其餘殆不足問。」

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: "Criminals and kin close by have already all died; the remainder scarcely merits inquiry."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "The criminals' close kin have already all been killed; the rest are hardly worth pursuing."

sentences.zh: 時宦官深怨李訓等，凡與之有瓜葛親，或暫蒙獎引者，誅貶不已，故二相言之。

translations.literal: At that time the eunuchs deeply hated Li Xun and the others; all who had any connection with them, or had briefly received their favor, were punished and demoted without end—therefore the two chief ministers spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs still hunted anyone tied to Xun; the two ministers spoke to curb the slaughter.

sentences.zh: 李訓、鄭注既誅，召六道巡邊使。

translations.literal: After Li Xun and Zheng Zhu had been executed, the six-circuit border patrol envoys were recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun and Zhu died, the six border envoys were recalled.

sentences.zh: 田全操追忿訓、注之謀，在道楊言：「我入城，凡儒服者，無貴賤當盡殺之！」

translations.literal: Tian Quancao, pursuing his rage at Xun and Zhu's plot on the road, proclaimed loudly: "When I enter the city, all who wear scholar's dress, without regard to noble or base, shall be killed to the last!"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Quancao, furious on the road, vowed, "When I reach the city I will kill every man in scholar's robes, high or low!"

sentences.zh: 癸未，全操等乘驛疾驅入金光門，京城訛言有寇至，士民驚噪縱橫走，塵埃四起。

translations.literal: On guiwei Quancao and the others drove post-horses at full speed through the Jinguang Gate; in the capital false reports spread that bandits had arrived; gentlemen and commoners panicked and ran in all directions, dust rising in four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Guiwei: Tian Quancao galloped through Jinguang Gate; rumor of attack sent the city fleeing in dust.

sentences.zh: 兩省諸司官聞之，皆奔散，有不及束帶襪而乘馬者。

translations.literal: Officials of the two departments and various bureaus heard it and all scattered in flight; some mounted horses without time to fasten belt or socks.
translations.idiomatic: Two-department officials fled; some rode off without belt or socks.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃、李石在中書，顧吏卒稍稍逃去。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan and Li Shi were in the Secretariat; they watched clerks and soldiers gradually escape.
translations.idiomatic: In the Secretariat, Zheng Tan and Li Shi watched clerks slip away.

sentences.zh: 覃謂石曰：「耳目頗異，宜且出避之！」

translations.literal: Tan said to Shi: "What we hear and see is rather unusual—we should for the moment go out and avoid it!"
translations.idiomatic: Tan told Shi, "Something is wrong—we should leave!"

sentences.zh: 石曰：「宰相位尊望重，人心所屬，不可輕也！

translations.literal: Shi said: "The chief minister's position is lofty and his weight heavy—he is what hearts rely on; he cannot be treated lightly!
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, "A chief minister is the people's anchor; he cannot run.

sentences.zh: 今事虛實未可知，堅坐鎮之，庶幾可定。

translations.literal: Today the affair's truth or falsehood is not yet known; sitting firm and calming it may perhaps settle things.
translations.idiomatic: Truth and rumor are unclear; sitting firm may steady the court.

sentences.zh: 若宰相亦走，則中外亂矣。

translations.literal: If the chief ministers also flee, then within and without there will be chaos.
translations.idiomatic: If ministers flee too, inside and outside will collapse.

sentences.zh: 且果有禍亂，避亦不免！」

translations.literal: And if there is truly calamity and disorder, to flee also cannot avoid it!"
translations.idiomatic: And if real chaos comes, flight will not save us."

sentences.zh: 覃然之。

translations.literal: Tan assented to this.
translations.idiomatic: Tan agreed.

sentences.zh: 石坐視文案，沛然自若。

translations.literal: Shi sat viewing documents, composed and at ease as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shi sat reviewing papers, outwardly calm.

sentences.zh: 敕使相繼傳呼：「閉皇城諸司門！」

translations.literal: Edict envoys came in succession calling out: "Close the gates of all offices in the Imperial City!"
translations.idiomatic: Messengers shouted in succession, "Close every gate of the Imperial City!"

sentences.zh: 左金吾大將軍陳君賞帥其眾立望仙門下，謂敕使曰：「賊至，閉門未晚，請徐觀其變，不宜示弱！」

translations.literal: The Left Gold Crow great general Chen Junshang led his troops to stand below Wangxian Gate and told the edict envoy: "When bandits arrive, it is not yet late to close the gate—please watch how things change at leisure; we should not show weakness!"
translations.idiomatic: Left Gold Crow general Chen Junshang massed his men at Wangxian Gate and told the messenger, "If rebels come, we can still shut the gate—watch how things unfold; do not show fear!"

sentences.zh: 至晡後乃定。

translations.literal: Not until after the hour of shen (late afternoon) did things settle.
translations.idiomatic: Calm did not return until late afternoon.

sentences.zh: 是日，坊市惡少年皆衣緋皁，持弓刀北望，見皇城門閉，即欲剽掠，非石與君賞鎮之，京城幾再亂矣。

translations.literal: That day, ruffian youths in the wards all wore scarlet and black, held bows and blades, and gazed north; seeing the Imperial City gates closed, they were about to plunder. Had Shi and Junshang not held them down, the capital would nearly have been thrown into chaos again.
translations.idiomatic: That day ward toughs in scarlet and black, armed with bow and blade, looked north; when the Imperial City gates closed they were ready to loot. Only Li Shi and Chen Junshang held the line—the capital nearly erupted again.

sentences.zh: 時兩省官應入直者，皆與其家人辭訣。

translations.literal: At that time, officials of the two departments who should report for palace duty all took farewell leave of their families.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of both departments due for palace duty bade their families farewell.

sentences.zh: 甲申，敕罷修曲江亭館。

translations.literal: On jiashen, an edict halted construction of Qujiang pavilions and lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Jiashen: an edict stopped work on Qujiang pavilions and lodges.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔：「逆人親黨，自非前已就戮及指名收捕者，餘一切不問。

translations.literal: On dinghai, an edict stated: "Relatives and partisans of the rebels—except those already executed before this or named for arrest—all will not be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Dinghai: an edict declared, "As for the rebels' kin and associates, except for those already executed or specifically named for arrest, all others are not to be pursued.

sentences.zh: 諸司官吏雖為所脅從，涉於詿誤，皆赦之。

translations.literal: Officials of various bureaus who were coerced to follow, implicated by mistaken involvement—all are pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau officials coerced into complicity or caught in error were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 他人毋得妄相告言及相恐惕。

translations.literal: Others must not recklessly inform on one another or intimidate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Others were forbidden to inform on or terrorize one another.

sentences.zh: 見亡匿者，勿復追捕，三日內各聽自歸本司。」

translations.literal: Those seen in hiding—do not pursue further; within three days each is permitted to return to his original bureau."
translations.idiomatic: Those now in flight or hiding are not to be pursued; within three days each may return to his original office."

sentences.zh: 時禁軍暴橫，京兆尹張仲方不敢詰，宰相以其不勝任，出為華州刺史，以司農卿薛元賞代之。

translations.literal: At that time the Palace Armies were violent and overbearing; Metropolitan Governor Zhang Zhongfang dared not investigate. The chief ministers, deeming him incompetent, sent him out as Huazhou prefectural governor and replaced him with Court of Imperial Granaries Director Xue Yuanshang.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Armies ran riot; Jingzhao governor Zhang Zhongfang dared not press them. The ministers removed him to Huazhou and installed granaries director Xue Yuanshang as metropolitan governor.

sentences.zh: 元賞常詣李石第，聞石方坐聽事與一人爭辯甚喧，元賞使覘之，雲有神策軍將訴事。

translations.literal: Yuanshang often visited Li Shi's residence; hearing Shi was sitting in the audience hall in heated argument with someone very loudly, Yuanshang had someone spy—it was said a Shence Army general was pressing a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshang often called on Li Shi and heard loud quarreling in the hall; inquiry showed a Shence general pressing a grievance.

sentences.zh: 元賞趨入，責石曰：「相公輔佐天子，紀綱四海。

translations.literal: Yuanshang hurried in and reproached Shi: "The chief minister assists the Son of Heaven and upholds discipline throughout the Four Seas.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshang rushed in and rebuked Shi: "You assist the Son of Heaven and govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 今近不能制一軍將，使無禮如此，何以鎮服四夷！」

translations.literal: Now in your own vicinity you cannot control a single army general, letting him be this disrespectful—how can you awe and subdue the four barbarians!"
translations.idiomatic: You cannot restrain one general under your nose—how will you awe the four quarters?"

sentences.zh: 即趨出上馬，命左右擒軍將，俟於下馬橋，元賞至，則已解衣跽之矣。

translations.literal: He immediately rushed out, mounted his horse, and ordered attendants to seize the army general, waiting at Xiamaqiao. When Yuanshang arrived, the man had already removed his upper garment and was kneeling in submission.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted at once, ordered the general seized at Xiamaqiao, and found him stripped and kneeling when he arrived.

sentences.zh: 其黨訴於仇士良，士良遣宦者召之曰：「中尉屈大尹。」

translations.literal: His faction complained to Qiu Shiliang; Shiliang sent a eunuch to summon him, saying: "The Defender humbles the metropolitan governor."
translations.idiomatic: His men appealed to Qiu Shiliang, who sent a eunuch: "The Defender yields to the metropolitan governor."

sentences.zh: 元賞曰：「屬有公事，行當繼至。」

translations.literal: Yuanshang said: "I have official business and will follow shortly."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshang replied, "Official business—I'll come directly."

sentences.zh: 遂杖殺之。

translations.literal: Then he had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Then he had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 乃白服見士良，士良曰：「癡書生何敢杖殺禁軍大將！」

translations.literal: He then went to see Shiliang in plain white dress; Shiliang said: "Foolish bookworm—how dare you beat to death a Palace Army great general!"
translations.idiomatic: He went to Shiliang in plain dress. Shiliang said, "Foolish scholar—how dare you beat a Palace Army general to death!"

sentences.zh: 元賞曰：「中尉大臣也，宰相亦大臣也，宰相之人若無禮於中尉，如之何？

translations.literal: Yuanshang said: "The Defender is a great minister and the chief minister is also a great minister. If the chief minister's man is disrespectful to the Defender, what then?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshang said, "The Defender is a great minister; so is the chief minister. If the minister's man insults the Defender, what then?

sentences.zh: 中尉之人無禮於宰相，庸可恕乎！

translations.literal: If the Defender's man is disrespectful to the chief minister, can that be forgiven!
translations.idiomatic: If the Defender's man insults the minister, can that be forgiven?

sentences.zh: 中尉與國同體，當為國惜法，元賞已囚服而來，惟中尉死生之！」

translations.literal: The Defender shares one body with the state and ought to cherish the law on the state's behalf. Yuanshang has come bound in humble dress—let the Defender dispose of my life or death!"
translations.idiomatic: The Defender is one with the state and should uphold its law. I come as a prisoner—do with me as you will!"

sentences.zh: 士良知軍將已死，無可如何，乃呼酒與元賞歡飲而罷。

translations.literal: Shiliang knew the army general was already dead and could do nothing; he called for wine and drank happily with Yuanshang, then they parted.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang knew the general was dead and could do nothing; he called for wine and drank with Yuanshang, then let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 初，武元衡之死，詔出內庫弓矢、陌刀給金吾仗，使衛從宰相，至建福門而退。

translations.literal: Initially, after Wu Yuanheng's death, an edict took bows, arrows, and mo blades from the inner treasury for the Gold Crow guard staffs to escort the chief ministers, withdrawing only at Jianfu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Yuanheng's murder, the court had issued inner-store bows, arrows, and mo blades to Gold Crow guards to escort chief ministers as far as Jianfu Gate.

sentences.zh: 至是，悉罷之。

translations.literal: By now all that was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Now that escort was abolished entirely.

sentences.zh: 文宗元聖昭獻孝皇帝中開成元年（

translations.literal: The first year of Kaicheng in the middle reign of Emperor Wenzong, Yuan Sheng Zhao Xian Filial Emperor (
translations.idiomatic: The first year of Kaicheng in the middle reign of Emperor Wenzong, the Yuan Sheng Zhao Xian Filial Emperor (

sentences.zh: 丙辰，公元八三六年）

translations.literal: bingchen, 836 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingchen, 836 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑朔，上御宣政殿，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on xinchou the first day of the month, the emperor entered Xuanzheng Hall, amnestied the realm, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, first month, xinchou new moon: the emperor took Xuanzheng Hall, amnestied the realm, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 仇士良請以神策仗衛殿門，諫議大夫馮定言其不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang asked to use Shence guard staffs to defend the hall gates; remonstrance official Feng Ding said it could not be done, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang sought Shence guards for the hall gates; remonstrance official Feng Ding objected, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 定，宿之弟也。

translations.literal: Ding was the younger brother of Su.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was Feng Su's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸未，上與宰相語，患四方表奏華而不典，李石對曰：「古人因事為文，今人以文害事。」

translations.literal: Second month, on guiwei, the emperor discussed with the chief ministers his distress that memorials from the four quarters were florid and not canonical. Li Shi replied: "The ancients produced writing because of events; today men harm affairs because of writing."
translations.idiomatic: Second month, guiwei: the emperor told ministers he was troubled by florid, uncanonical memorials from the provinces. Li Shi said, "Antiquity wrote from events; today writing harms affairs."

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使劉從諫上表請王涯等罪名，且言：「涯等儒生，荷國榮龐，鹹欲保身全族，安肯構逆！

translations.literal: Zhaoyi military commissioner Liu Congjian memorialized requesting the crimes of Wang Ya and others, and said: "Ya and the others were Confucian scholars bearing national honor and splendor; they all wished to preserve body and clan—how would they scheme rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi commissioner Liu Congjian memorialized on Wang Ya's crimes, saying, "Ya and his fellows were scholars honored by the state; they sought only to save themselves and their kin—why rebel?

sentences.zh: 訓等實欲討除內臣，兩中尉自為救死之謀，遂致相殺，誣以反逆，誠恐非辜。

translations.literal: Xun and the others truly wished to eliminate the inner attendants; the two defenders made plans to save their own lives, thus bringing mutual slaughter, slandering them with rebellion—truly fearing they were not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Xun truly aimed at the eunuchs; the two defenders fought for their lives, then slaughtered each other and branded them rebels—I fear they were innocent.

sentences.zh: 設右宰相實有異圖，當委之有司，正其刑典，豈有內臣擅領甲兵，恣行剽劫，延及士庶，橫被殺傷！

translations.literal: Suppose the chief ministers on the right truly had a different design—they should have been entrusted to the proper offices to rectify them by statute. How could inner attendants on their own lead armored troops, wantonly plunder, extend harm to gentlemen and commoners, and kill and wound at will!
translations.idiomatic: If the chief ministers truly plotted treason, the law should judge them—how could eunuchs lead troops, loot at will, and slaughter officials and commoners!

sentences.zh: 流血千門，殭屍萬計，搜羅枝蔓，中外恫疑。

translations.literal: Blood flowed at a thousand gates; corpses numbered in the tens of thousands; branches and tendrils were hunted down; within and without were shaken in fear and doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Blood ran at a thousand gates; corpses piled by the ten thousand; networks were hunted; court and country trembled.

sentences.zh: 臣欲身詣闕庭，面陳臧否，恐並陷孥戮，事亦無成。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to go in person to the court gate and face the emperor to state right and wrong, but fears being destroyed together with wife and children—the affair would also come to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: I would go to court in person to speak truth to power, but fear my family would perish with me and nothing would be gained.

sentences.zh: 謹當修飾封疆，訓練士卒，內為陛下心腹，外為陛下籓垣。

translations.literal: I will respectfully repair and adorn my borders, train soldiers and horsemen, inwardly serve Your Majesty as heart and belly, outwardly serve Your Majesty as rampart and wall.
translations.idiomatic: I shall ready my borders and train my troops—to be Your Majesty's heart within and bulwark without.

sentences.zh: 如奸臣難制，誓以死清君側！」

translations.literal: If treacherous ministers are hard to control, I vow to die cleansing the ruler's side!"
translations.idiomatic: If wicked ministers cannot be checked, I swear to die purging the ruler's side!"

sentences.zh: 丙申，加從諫檢校司徒。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Congjian was given the additional title of acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Bingshen: Congjian was made acting Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 天德軍奏吐谷渾三千帳詣豐州降。

translations.literal: The Tiande Army reported that three thousand Tuyuhun households came to Fengzhou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tiande Army reported three thousand Tuyuhun households surrendering at Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬寅，以袁州長史李德裕為水除州刺史。

translations.literal: Third month, on renyin, Yuanzhou senior administrator Li Deyu was made prefectural governor of Shuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, renyin: Yuanzhou senior administrator Li Deyu was appointed prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 左僕射令狐楚從容奏：「王涯等既伏辜，其家夷滅，遺骸棄捐。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Linghu Chu calmly memorialized: "Wang Ya and the others having already paid guilt, their families were exterminated and their remains cast away.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice director Linghu Chu gently urged, "Wang Ya and the others have paid with their lives; their families are gone and their bones lie abandoned.

sentences.zh: 請官為收瘞，以順陽和之氣。」

translations.literal: I ask that the government collect and bury them, to accord with the yang and harmonious qi."
translations.idiomatic: Let the state gather and bury them, in keeping with spring's gentle qi."

sentences.zh: 上慘然久之，命京兆收葬涯等十一人於城西，各賜衣一襲。

translations.literal: The emperor was somber a long while, then ordered Jingzhao to collect and bury Ya and eleven others west of the city, each granted one suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved long, then ordered Jingzhao to bury Ya and eleven others west of the city, each granted a suit of mourning clothes.

sentences.zh: 仇士良潛使人發之，棄骨於渭水。

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang secretly sent men to exhume them and cast the bones into the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang secretly had the graves opened and the bones thrown into the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 丁未，皇城留守郭皎奏：「諸司儀仗有鋒刃者，請皆輸軍器使，遇立仗別給儀刀！」

translations.literal: On dingwei, Imperial City garrison commander Guo Jiao memorialized: "Among the ceremonial regalia of various offices, those with sharp edges—please have them all delivered to the Armory Commissioner; when standing guard, issue separate ceremonial blades!"
translations.idiomatic: Dingwei: Imperial City commander Guo Jiao memorialized, "All ceremonial weapons in the various offices that have sharp edges should be turned over to the Armory Commissioner; when standing guard, separate ceremonial blades should be issued!"

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 劉從諫復遣牙將焦楚長上表讓官，稱：「臣之所陳，系國大體。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian again sent military adjutant Jiao Chuchang to memorialize declining the office, stating: "What your servant stated concerns the great substance of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian again sent adjutant Jiao Chuchang to decline his promotion, saying, "My plea concerns the fate of the realm.

sentences.zh: 可聽則涯等宜蒙湔洗，不可聽則賞典不宜妄加！

translations.literal: If heeded, then Ya and the others ought to receive cleansing; if not heeded, then reward statutes ought not be recklessly bestowed!
translations.idiomatic: If you heed me, clear Wang Ya's name; if not, do not lavish rewards on me!

sentences.zh: 安有死冤不申而生者荷祿！」

translations.literal: How can there be the dead with unredressed wrongs while the living bear salary!
translations.idiomatic: How can the dead lie wronged while the living draw salary!"

sentences.zh: 因暴揚仇士良等罪惡。

translations.literal: He thereby openly exposed the crimes of Qiu Shiliang and others.
translations.idiomatic: He openly denounced the crimes of Qiu Shiliang and his faction.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，上召見楚長，慰諭遣之。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the emperor summoned Chuchang, comforted and instructed him, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Xinyou: the emperor received Chuchang, comforted him, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 時士良等恣橫，朝臣日憂破家。

translations.literal: At that time Shiliang and the others were wanton and overbearing; court officials daily feared the ruin of their families.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang and his men ran rampant; officials daily feared their families would be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 及從諫表至，士良等憚之。

translations.literal: When Congjian's memorial arrived, Shiliang and the others feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Congjian's memorial arrived, Shiliang and his faction were afraid.

sentences.zh: 由是鄭覃、李石粗能秉政，天子倚之亦差以自強。

translations.literal: From this Zheng Tan and Li Shi were roughly able to hold power; the Son of Heaven relied on them and also gained somewhat in self-strengthening.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Zheng Tan and Li Shi could roughly govern; the emperor leaned on them and regained some strength.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己卯，以潮州司戶李宗閔為衡州司馬。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on jimao, Chaozhou registrar Li Zongmin was made Hengzhou militia adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, jimao: Chaozhou registrar Li Zongmin was made Hengzhou militia adjutant.

sentences.zh: 凡李訓所指為李德裕、宗閔黨者，稍收復之。

translations.literal: All whom Li Xun had marked as partisans of Li Deyu and Zongmin were gradually restored.
translations.idiomatic: Those Li Xun had branded as Li Deyu or Zongmin partisans were gradually restored to office.

sentences.zh: 淄王協薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Zi, Xie, died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xie of Zi died.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以山南西道節度使李固言為門下侍郎、同平章事，以左僕射令狐楚代之。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Shannan West Circuit military commissioner Li Guyan was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Chief Minister; Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Linghu Chu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiawu: Shannan West commissioner Li Guyan became vice director of the Chancellery and associate chief minister; Linghu Chu replaced him as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，上與宰相從容論詩之工拙，鄭覃曰：「詩之工者，無若三百篇，皆國人作之以刺美時政，王者采之以觀風俗耳，不聞王者為詩也。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the emperor discussed with the chief ministers at leisure the skill and clumsiness of poetry. Zheng Tan said: "In skilled poetry nothing surpasses the three hundred pieces—all were made by the people of the states to satirize and praise current government; the king gathered them to observe customs—that is all; one does not hear of kings making poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxu: the emperor chatted with ministers about poetry. Zheng Tan said, "Nothing matches the Odes—commoners wrote them to praise or satirize government; kings collected them to read the mood of the realm. Kings do not write poetry.

sentences.zh: 後代辭人之詩，華而不實，無補於事。

translations.literal: The poetry of later generations' literary men is florid without substance and of no help to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later poets' verse is florid and empty—it does not help govern.

sentences.zh: 陳後主、隋煬帝皆工於詩，不免亡國，陛下何取焉！」

translations.literal: Chen Last Ruler and Sui Emperor Yang were both skilled at poetry, yet could not avoid losing the state—what does Your Majesty take from them!"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Houzhu and Sui Yangdi were fine poets—and lost their realms. What is there to emulate?"

sentences.zh: 覃篤於經術，上甚重之。

translations.literal: Tan was devoted to classical learning; the emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was steeped in the classics; the emperor valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 己酉，上御紫宸殿，宰相因奏事拜謝，外間因訛言：「天子欲令宰相掌禁兵，已拜恩矣。」

translations.literal: On jiyou, the emperor entered Zichen Hall; the chief ministers, because of presenting affairs, bowed in thanks. Outside, because of false reports: "The Son of Heaven wishes to have the chief ministers command the Palace Armies—they have already received the grace of appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Jiyou: at Zichen Hall the ministers bowed after audience. Rumor spread: "The emperor has put the ministers in charge of the Palace Armies, and they have already accepted the commission."

sentences.zh: 由是中外復有猜阻，人情恟恟，士民不敢解衣寢者數日。

translations.literal: From this within and without there was again suspicion and obstruction; people's hearts were in uproar; gentlemen and commoners did not dare undress to sleep for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion spread through court and city; panic reigned; for days people slept in their clothes.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，李石奏請召仇士良等面釋其疑。

translations.literal: On yichou, Li Shi memorialized requesting that Qiu Shiliang and the others be summoned to dispel their doubts face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Yichou: Li Shi asked that Qiu Shiliang and the others be summoned to clear the misunderstanding face to face.

sentences.zh: 上為召士良等出，上及石等共諭釋之，使毋疑懼，然後事解。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Shiliang and the others forth; the emperor together with Shi and the others jointly instructed and released them, making them not doubt or fear—only then was the affair resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Shiliang and his men; he and Li Shi reassured them until fear subsided and calm returned.

sentences.zh: 閏月，乙酉，以太子太保、分司李聽為河中節度使。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, on yiyou, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and commissioner in absentia Li Ting was made Hezhong military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary month, yiyou: retired grand mentor Li Ting was made Hezhong military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上常歎曰：「付之兵不疑，置之散地不怨，惟聽為可以然。」

translations.literal: The emperor often sighed and said: "Entrust him with troops and he does not doubt; place him in a scattered post and he does not resent—only Ting can be thus."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often said, "Give him an army and he is loyal; set him aside and he does not complain—only Li Ting can do that."

sentences.zh: 乙未，李固言薦崔球為起居舍人，鄭覃再三以為不可，上曰：「公事勿相違！」

translations.literal: On yiwei, Li Guyan recommended Cui Qiu as Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Residence; Zheng Tan repeatedly said it could not be done. The emperor said: "On public business do not oppose one another!"
translations.idiomatic: Yiwei: Li Guyan recommended Cui Qiu as palace attendant; Zheng Tan objected repeatedly. The emperor said, "On state business, do not simply oppose each other!"

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「若宰相盡同，則事必有欺陛下者矣！」

translations.literal: Tan said: "If the chief ministers are all alike, then in affairs there will surely be someone deceiving Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "If ministers always agree, someone is surely deceiving Your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 李孝本二女配沒右軍，上取之入宮。

translations.literal: Li Xiaoben's two daughters, confiscated and assigned to the Right Army, the emperor took them into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Two daughters of Li Xiaoben, confiscated to the Right Army, were taken into the palace by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，右拾遺魏謨上疏，以為：「陛下不邇聲色，屢出宮女以配鰥夫。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Right Reminder Wei Mo submitted a memorial, stating: "Your Majesty does not draw near to sound and color, and has repeatedly released palace women to match with widowers.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month: Right Reminder Wei Mo memorialized, "Your Majesty keeps away from pleasure and has repeatedly released palace women to marry widowers.

sentences.zh: 竊聞數月以來，教坊選試以百數，莊宅收市猶未已；

translations.literal: I have heard that for several months the Music Office has selected and tested by the hundreds, and the Crown Estate's purchases in the market have not yet ceased;
translations.idiomatic: Yet for months the Music Office has auditioned hundreds, and the Crown Estate still buys in the markets;

sentences.zh: 又召李孝本女入宮，不避宗姓，大興物論，臣竊惜之。

translations.literal: again you summoned Li Xiaoben's daughter into the palace, not avoiding the imperial clan surname—greatly stirring public discussion. Your servant privately regrets this.
translations.idiomatic: you also took Li Xiaoben's daughter into the palace without regard for her imperial surname—scandal spreads. I grieve to see it.

sentences.zh: 昔漢光武一顧列女屏風，宋弘猶正色抗言，光武即撤之。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Han Emperor Guangwu once glanced at the screen of exemplary women, Song Hong still sternly remonstrated face to face, and Guangwu immediately removed it.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Guangwu once glanced at a screen of exemplary women, Song Hong rebuked him to his face—and Guangwu had it removed at once.

sentences.zh: 陛下豈可不思宋弘之言，欲居光武之下乎！」

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty not reflect on Song Hong's words—does he wish to rank below Guangwu!"
translations.idiomatic: Will Your Majesty not heed Song Hong—and rank below Guangwu?"

sentences.zh: 上即出孝本女。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately released Xiaoben's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once sent Xiaoben's daughter out of the palace.

sentences.zh: 擢謨為補闕，曰：「朕選市女子，以賜諸王耳。

translations.literal: He promoted Mo to Reminder and said: "We select market women to bestow on the princes—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Mo to Reminder and said, "I was only choosing market women to give to the princes.

sentences.zh: 憐孝本女宗枝髫齔孤露，故收養宮中。

translations.literal: Pitying Xiaoben's daughter of the imperial clan branch, in infancy and exposed in orphanhood, I therefore took her in to raise in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: I pitied Xiaoben's daughter—a young orphan of the imperial clan—and took her into the palace to raise her.

sentences.zh: 謨於疑似之間皆能盡言，可謂愛我，不忝厥祖矣！」

translations.literal: Mo in matters of doubt and resemblance can speak fully—he may be called one who loves Us and does not disgrace his ancestors!"
translations.idiomatic: Mo speaks plainly even on delicate matters—he truly loves me and honors his ancestors!"

sentences.zh: 命中書優為制辭以賞之。

translations.literal: He ordered the Secretariat to compose an excellent edict of praise to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Secretariat to draft a generous commendation.

sentences.zh: 謨，征之五世孫也。

translations.literal: Mo was a fifth-generation descendant of Wei Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was a fifth-generation descendant of Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 鄜坊節度使蕭洪詐稱太后弟，事覺。

translations.literal: Binfang military commissioner Xiao Hong falsely claimed to be the empress dowager's younger brother; the affair was discovered.
translations.idiomatic: Binfang commissioner Xiao Hong falsely claimed to be the empress dowager's brother; the fraud was exposed.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲辰，流驩州，於道賜死。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on jiachen, he was banished to Huanzhou and on the road was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, jiachen: he was exiled to Huanzhou and ordered to die on the road.

sentences.zh: 趙縝、呂璋等皆流嶺南。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhen, Lü Zhang, and others were all banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhen, Lü Zhang, and others were all exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 初，李訓知洪之詐，洪懼，辟訓兄仲京置幕府。

translations.literal: Initially, Li Xun knew of Hong's fraud; Hong was afraid and recruited Xun's elder brother Zhongjing to place in his staff headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun knew Hong was a fraud; Hong, afraid, hired Xun's brother Zhongjing for his staff.

sentences.zh: 先是，自神策軍出為節度使者，軍中皆資其行裝，至鎮，三倍償之。

translations.literal: Before this, when men left the Shence Army to become military commissioners, the army all supplied their travel expenses; on reaching their command, they repaid threefold.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, Shence officers posted as commissioners were advanced travel funds by the army and repaid triple on reaching their posts.

sentences.zh: 有自左軍出鎮鄜坊未償而死者，軍中征之於洪，洪恃訓之勢，不與。

translations.literal: There was one who left the Left Army to take command of Binfang, died before repaying, and the army demanded payment from Hong; Hong relied on Xun's power and would not pay.
translations.idiomatic: A Left Army man posted to Binfang died before repaying his debt; the army demanded payment from Hong, who refused, counting on Li Xun's backing.

sentences.zh: 又征於死者之子，洪教其子遮宰相自言，訓判絕之。

translations.literal: They again demanded payment from the dead man's son; Hong taught the son to block the chief minister and speak for himself—Xun ruled and cut him off.
translations.idiomatic: They then pressed the dead man's son; Hong had the son waylay the chief minister to plead; Xun ruled against him.

sentences.zh: 仇士良由是恨洪。

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang from this hated Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang therefore hated Hong.

sentences.zh: 太后有異母弟在閩中，孱弱不能自達。

translations.literal: The empress dowager had a younger half-brother in Min, frail and unable to make himself known.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had a weak half-brother in Fujian who could not reach court on his own.

sentences.zh: 有閩人蕭本從之得其內外族諱，因士良進達於上，且發洪之詐，洪由是得罪。

translations.literal: A man of Min, Xiao Ben, followed him and obtained the inner and outer clan taboo names; through Shiliang he advanced to reach the emperor, and also exposed Hong's fraud—Hong from this was punished.
translations.idiomatic: A Fujianese named Xiao Ben learned the clan taboo names, reached the emperor through Shiliang, and exposed Hong's fraud—Hong fell.

sentences.zh: 上以本為真太后弟，戊申，擢為右贊善大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor took Ben as the empress dowager's true younger brother; on wushen he was promoted to Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Ben as the empress dowager's true brother; wushen: he was made right mentor of the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁丑，李石為上言宋申錫忠直，為讒人所誣，竄死遐荒，未蒙昭雪。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on dingchou, Li Shi spoke to the emperor of Song Shenxi's loyalty and uprightness, how slanderers had falsely accused him, how he was banished and died in distant wilds, and had not received clearing of his name.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, dingchou: Li Shi told the emperor that Song Shenxi had been loyal and upright, slandered into exile and death in the wilderness, and never vindicated.

sentences.zh: 上俯首久之，既而流涕泫然曰：「茲事朕久知其誤，奸人逼我，以社稷大計，兄弟幾不能保，況申錫，僅全腰領耳。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed his head a long while, then wept with streaming tears and said: "In this affair I have long known it was wrong. Wicked men pressed me; for the great plan of altars and state, my brothers could barely be preserved—how much less Shenxi, who merely kept his waist and neck intact.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed his head long, then wept: "I have long known this was wrong. Villains forced me—for the realm's sake my own brothers barely survived; Shenxi was lucky to keep his head.

sentences.zh: 非獨內臣，外廷亦有助之者。

translations.literal: It was not only the inner attendants—those outside the court also had helpers.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs were not alone—men of the outer court helped them.

sentences.zh: 皆由朕之不明，向使遇漢昭帝，必無此冤矣！」

translations.literal: All was because of Our lack of clarity—had We met Han Emperor Zhaodi, there would surely have been no such injustice!"
translations.idiomatic: It was all my blindness—had I been like Han Zhaodi, this injustice would never have happened!"

sentences.zh: 鄭覃、李固言亦共言其冤，上深痛恨，有慚色。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan and Li Guyan also jointly spoke of his injustice; the emperor deeply hated and regretted it, showing an ashamed countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan and Li Guyan also pleaded his injustice; the emperor was filled with bitter remorse and showed shame.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔悉復申錫官爵，以其子慎微為成固尉。

translations.literal: On gengchen, an edict fully restored Shenxi's offices and titles, making his son Shenwei an assistant magistrate of Chenggu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen an edict fully restored Shenxi's rank and titles and appointed his son Shenwei assistant magistrate of Chenggu.

sentences.zh: 李石用金部員外郎韓益判度支，案益坐贓三千餘緡，繫獄。

translations.literal: Li Shi employed Jin Bu Vice Director Han Yi as acting fiscal commissioner of the Revenue Circuit; when the case was investigated Yi was found guilty of embezzling more than three thousand strings of cash and was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi put Jin Bu vice director Han Yi in charge of fiscal affairs; an investigation found Yi guilty of embezzling more than three thousand strings of cash, and he was jailed.

sentences.zh: 石曰：「臣始以益頗曉錢穀，故用之，不知其貪乃如是！」

translations.literal: Shi said: "Your subject at first thought Yi was quite knowledgeable about revenue and grain, and so employed him—I did not know his greed would be like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "I first thought Yi knew revenue well and put him to work—I never dreamed he was this corrupt!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「宰相但知人則用，有過則懲，如此則人易得。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Chancellor, if you know a man then employ him; if there is fault then punish—thus men are easy to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A chancellor need only employ those he knows and punish their faults—that is how good men are found.

sentences.zh: 卿所用人不掩其惡，可謂至公。

translations.literal: The men you employ—you do not cover their evil; this can be called utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: You do not cover your appointees' wrongdoing—that is true impartiality.

sentences.zh: 從前宰相用人好曲蔽其過，不欲人彈劾，此大病也。」

translations.literal: Former chancellors when employing men liked to bend and conceal their faults, not wanting people to impeach—this was a great ill."
translations.idiomatic: Past chancellors bent the rules to hide their men's faults and blocked impeachment—that was a grave evil."

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，丁巳，貶益梧州司戶。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, on dingsi, Yi was demoted to assistant prefectural secretary of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, eleventh month, dingsi: Yi was demoted to assistant prefectural secretary of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 上自甘露之變，意忽忽不樂，兩軍球鞠之會什減六七，雖宴享音伎雜遝盈庭，未嘗解顏。
