translations.literal: Since the Sweet Dew coup the emperor's mind was restless and unhappy; cuju matches of the two armies were reduced by six or seven tenths; though feasts and music filled the court, he never once relaxed his face.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Sweet Dew coup the emperor had been restless and downcast; cuju matches of the two armies fell by six or seven tenths, and though feasts and musicians crowded the hall, he never once smiled.

sentences.zh: 閒居或徘徊眺望，或獨語歎息。

translations.literal: At leisure he would sometimes pace and gaze into the distance, sometimes speak alone and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: In private he would pace and stare into the distance, or murmur and sigh alone.

sentences.zh: 壬午，上於延英謂宰相曰：「朕每與卿等論天下事，則不免愁。」

translations.literal: On renwu at Yingying the emperor told the chancellors: "Every time We discuss affairs under Heaven with you, We cannot avoid sorrow."
translations.idiomatic: On renwu at Yingying the emperor told the chancellors, "Whenever I discuss the realm with you, sorrow follows."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「為理者不可以速成。」

translations.literal: They replied: "One who governs cannot expect quick completion."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Good government cannot be rushed."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「聯每讀書，恥為凡主。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Whenever I read books, I am ashamed to be a mediocre ruler."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Whenever I read, I am ashamed to be an ordinary sovereign."

sentences.zh: 李石曰：「方今內外之臣，其間小人尚多疑阻，願陛下更以寬御之，彼有公清奉法如劉弘逸、薛季稜者，陛下亦宜褒賞以勸為善。」

translations.literal: Li Shi said: "Today among inner and outer officials, petty men still cast much suspicion and obstruction; may Your Majesty govern them with greater leniency. Those who are upright and law-abiding like Liu Hongyi and Xue Jiling—Your Majesty should also praise and reward them to encourage goodness."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi said, "Petty men inside and outside court still sow suspicion and obstruction; I beg Your Majesty to govern with greater leniency. Men as upright and law-abiding as Liu Hongyi and Xue Jiling should also be praised and rewarded to encourage others."

sentences.zh: 甲申，上復謂宰相曰：「我與卿等論天下事，有勢未得行者，退但飲醇酒求醉耳！」

translations.literal: On jiashen the emperor again told the chancellors: "When I discuss affairs under Heaven with you, there are matters the situation will not let me carry out—on retiring I can only drink strong wine to seek drunkenness!"
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the emperor again told the chancellors, "When we discuss the realm, some plans circumstances will not let me execute—on leaving I can only drink myself drunk!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此皆臣等之罪也。」

translations.literal: They replied: "This is all our ministers' fault."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "That is our fault alone."

sentences.zh: 有司以左藏積弊日久，請行檢勘，且言官典罪在赦前者，請宥之，上許之。

translations.literal: The relevant offices, citing long-standing abuses in the Left Treasury, requested an audit; they also said that officials guilty before an amnesty should be pardoned—the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices, citing long-standing abuses in the Left Treasury, requested an audit and asked that officials guilty before an amnesty be pardoned; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而果得繒帛妄稱漬污者，敕赦之。

translations.literal: Soon they truly found silk goods falsely claimed as stained; an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The audit soon turned up silk falsely claimed as water-stained; an edict pardoned the guilty.

sentences.zh: 給事中狄兼謨封還敕書曰：「官典犯贓，理不可赦！」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Di Jianmo returned the edict sealed, saying: "Officials guilty of embezzlement—in principle cannot be pardoned!"
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Di Jianmo returned the edict unopened, saying, "Corrupt officials must not be pardoned!"

sentences.zh: 上諭之曰：「有司請檢之初，聯既許之矣。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him: "At the outset when the offices requested the audit, I had already consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "When the offices first asked for the audit, I had already promised amnesty.

sentences.zh: 與其失信，寧失罪人。

translations.literal: Rather break faith, than lose the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather let the guilty go free than break the promise I already made.

sentences.zh: 卿能奉職，朕甚嘉之！」

translations.literal: You can fulfill your duty—We greatly commend you!"
translations.idiomatic: You have done your duty—I commend you warmly!"

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚戌，以華州刺史盧鈞為嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on gengxu, Huazhou Governor Lu Jun was made Lingnan Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, gengxu: Huazhou governor Lu Jun was made military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 李石言於上曰：「盧鈞除嶺南，朝士皆相賀。

translations.literal: Li Shi spoke to the emperor, saying: "When Lu Jun was appointed to Lingnan, courtiers all congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi told the emperor, "When Lu Jun was posted to Lingnan, the court congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 以為嶺南富饒之地，近歲皆厚賂北司而得之；

translations.literal: They took Lingnan to be a rich and fertile region; in recent years all had obtained it by heavy bribes to the Northern Office;
translations.idiomatic: They took Lingnan for a rich post that in recent years men had bought with heavy bribes to the Northern Office;

sentences.zh: 今北司不撓朝權，陛下宜有以褒之。

translations.literal: now the Northern Office does not interfere in court power—Your Majesty ought to reward him suitably.
translations.idiomatic: now that the Northern Office no longer meddles in court affairs, Your Majesty should reward him.

sentences.zh: 庶幾內外奉法，此致理之本也。」

translations.literal: Then perhaps inner and outer will observe the law—this is the root of attaining good order."
translations.idiomatic: Then perhaps inner and outer court will keep the law—that is the foundation of good government."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 鈞至鎮，以清惠著名。

translations.literal: Jun reached his post and was famed for purity and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun reached his post he won fame for integrity and kindness.

sentences.zh: 己未，淑王縱薨。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Prince Shu Zong died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiwei: Prince Shu Zong died.

sentences.zh: 文宗元聖昭獻孝皇帝中開成二年（

translations.literal: The second year of Kaicheng in the middle reign of Emperor Wenzong, Yuan Sheng Zhao Xian Filial Emperor (
translations.idiomatic: The second year of Kaicheng in the middle reign of Emperor Wenzong, the Yuan Sheng Zhao Xian Filial Emperor (

sentences.zh: 丁巳，公元八三七年）

translations.literal: dingsi, corresponding to the year 837 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingsi, corresponding to 837 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，己未，上謂宰相：「薦人勿問親疏，聯聞竇易直為相，未嘗用親故。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, on jiwei, the emperor told the chancellors: "When recommending men do not ask whether kin or distant—I have heard that when Dou Yizhi was chancellor he never employed kin or old associates.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, second month, jiwei: the emperor told the chancellors, "Recommend men without regard to kinship—I hear Dou Yizhi as chancellor never favored relatives.

sentences.zh: 若親故果才，避嫌而棄之，是亦不為至公也。」

translations.literal: If kin or old associates are truly talented, to avoid suspicion and discard them is also not utmost fairness."
translations.idiomatic: If a relative is truly able, to pass him over from squeamishness is not true fairness either."

sentences.zh: 均王緯薨。

translations.literal: Prince Jun Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun Wei died.

sentences.zh: 三月，有慧星出於張，長八丈餘。

translations.literal: Third month, a comet appeared in the Zhang constellation, more than eight zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: Third month: a comet appeared in the Zhang asterism, more than eight zhang in length.

sentences.zh: 壬申，詔撤樂減膳，以一日之分充十日。

translations.literal: On renshen, an edict withdrew music and reduced meals, stretching one day's portion over ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Renshen: an edict halted music and cut meals, spreading one day's ration over ten.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲辰，上對中書舍人、翰林學士兼侍書柳公權等於便殿，上舉衫袖示之曰：「此衣已三浣矣！」

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on jiachen, the emperor received Secretariat Drafter, Hanlin Academician, and attendant calligrapher Liu Gongquan and others in the side hall; the emperor raised his robe sleeve to show them and said: "This garment has already been washed three times!"
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, jiachen: in the side hall the emperor received drafter and Hanlin academician Liu Gongquan and others, held up his sleeve, and said, "This robe has been washed three times!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆美上之儉德，公權獨無言。

translations.literal: All praised the emperor's frugal virtue; Gongquan alone said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: All praised the emperor's thrift; Gongquan alone kept silent.

sentences.zh: 上問其故，對曰：「陛下貴為天子，富有四海，當進賢退不肖，納諫諍，明賞罰，乃可以致雍熙。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Your Majesty is exalted as Son of Heaven and possesses all within the four seas—you ought to advance the worthy and dismiss the unworthy, accept remonstrance, and clarify rewards and punishments; only thus can great peace be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he replied, "Your Majesty is Son of Heaven and owns the realm—you should promote the worthy, dismiss the unfit, heed remonstrance, and make rewards and punishments clear; that is how peace is won.

sentences.zh: 服浣濯之農，乃末節耳。」

translations.literal: Wearing washed clothes is but a trifling matter."
translations.idiomatic: Wearing washed clothes is a trifle."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「聯知舍人不應復為諫議，以卿有諍臣風采，須屈卿為之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I know a drafter ought not again serve as remonstrator—but because you have a censor's bearing, I must humble you to the post."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I know a drafter should not double as remonstrator—but you have a censor's bearing, so I must bend you to the role."

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以公權為諫議大夫，餘如故。

translations.literal: On yisi, Gongquan was made Remonstrance Grand Master; the rest of his posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yisi: Gongquan was made remonstrance grand master; his other posts were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以翰林學士、工部侍郎陳夷行同平章事。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Hanlin Academician and Works Vice Minister Chen Yixing was made Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxu: Hanlin academician and Works vice minister Chen Yixing was made associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 六月，河陽軍亂，節度使李泳奔懷州。

translations.literal: Sixth month, the Heyang army mutinied; Military Governor Li Yong fled to Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: the Heyang garrison mutinied and military governor Li Yong fled to Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 軍士焚腐署，殺泳二子，大掠數日方止。

translations.literal: The soldiers burned the granary offices, killed Yong's two sons, and plundered greatly for several days before it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The troops burned the granaries, killed Yong's two sons, and looted for days before order returned.

sentences.zh: 泳，長安市人，寓籍禁軍，以賂得方鎮。

translations.literal: Yong was a man of Chang'an, registered with the palace armies, and obtained a frontier command through bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was a Chang'an man on the palace-army rolls who had bought a frontier command with bribes.

sentences.zh: 所至恃所交結，貪殘不法，其不下堪命，故作亂。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he relied on his connections, was greedy, cruel, and unlawful; his subordinates could not bear his commands—hence the mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he went he leaned on his connections, plundered lawlessly, and drove his men past endurance—hence the revolt.

sentences.zh: 丁未，貶泳澧州長史。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Yong was demoted to chief secretary of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dingwei: Yong was demoted to chief secretary of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以左金吾將軍李執方為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: On wushen, Left Golden Crow Guard General Li Zhifang was made Heyang Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Wushen: Left Golden Crow guard general Li Zhifang was made military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸亥，振武奏党項三百餘帳剽掠逃去。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on guihai, Zhenwu reported that more than three hundred Tangut tents had raided and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, guihai: Zhenwu reported that more than three hundred Tangut tents had raided and fled.

sentences.zh: 給事中韋溫為太子侍讀，晨詣東宮，日中乃得見。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wei Wen served as Reader to the Heir Apparent; he went to the Eastern Palace in the morning but only saw him at midday.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wei Wen was reader to the crown prince; he called at the Eastern Palace at dawn but was not received until noon.

sentences.zh: 溫諫曰：「太子當雞鳴而起，問安視膳，不宜專事宴安！」

translations.literal: Wen remonstrated, saying: "The Heir Apparent ought to rise at cockcrow, inquire after health and inspect meals—he should not devote himself solely to feasting and comfort!"
translations.idiomatic: Wen remonstrated, "The crown prince should rise at cockcrow, inquire after the emperor's health, and attend his meals—not live for pleasure alone!"

sentences.zh: 太子不能用其言，溫乃辭侍讀。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent could not employ his words; Wen thereupon resigned as Reader.
translations.idiomatic: The prince would not heed him, and Wen resigned as reader.

sentences.zh: 辛未，罷守本官。

translations.literal: On xinwei, he was dismissed and kept his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Xinwei: he was relieved of the readership and kept his original post.

sentences.zh: 振武突厥百五十帳叛，剽掠營田。

translations.literal: At Zhenwu one hundred fifty Turkish tents rebelled and raided garrison farms.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenwu one hundred fifty Turkish tents rebelled and raided garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，節度使劉沔擊破之。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Military Governor Liu Mian defeated and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyin: military governor Liu Mian defeated them.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚戌，以昭儀王氏為德妃，昭容楊氏為賢妃。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on gengxu, Brilliant Consort Lady Wang was made Virtuous Consort and Accomplished Consort Lady Yang was made Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, gengxu: brilliant consort Lady Wang was made virtuous consort and accomplished consort Lady Yang was made worthy consort.

sentences.zh: 立敬宗之子休復為梁王，執中為襄王，言楊為杞王，成美為成王。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong's sons were established: Xiufu as Prince of Liang, Zhizhong as Prince of Xiang, Yanyang as Prince of Qi, and Chengmei as Prince of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong's sons Xiufu, Zhizhong, Yanyang, and Chengmei were made princes of Liang, Xiang, Qi, and Cheng.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，立皇子宗儉為蔣王。

translations.literal: On guichou, the imperial son Zongjian was established as Prince of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guichou: the prince Zongjian was made Prince of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 河陽軍士既逐李泳，日相扇，欲為亂。

translations.literal: After the Heyang soldiers had expelled Li Yong, day by day they incited one another, intending mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: After expelling Li Yong, the Heyang troops incited one another daily and plotted further trouble.

sentences.zh: 九月，李執方索得首亂者七十餘人，悉斬之，餘黨分隸外鎮，然後定。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Li Zhifang tracked down more than seventy ringleaders and beheaded them all; the rest of the party were assigned to outer commands—only then was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Li Zhifang seized more than seventy ringleaders and executed them; the rest were scattered to other commands, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，國子監《石經》成。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, the Directorate of Education's Stone Classics were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month: the Directorate of Education's Stone Classics were completed.

sentences.zh: 福建奏晉江百姓蕭弘稱太后族人，詔御史台案之。

translations.literal: Fujian reported that Jinjiang commoner Xiao Hong claimed to be kin of the empress dowager; an edict ordered the Censorate to investigate the case.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian reported that a Jinjiang commoner named Xiao Hong claimed kinship with the empress dowager; the Censorate was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以門下侍郎、同平章事李固言同平章事，充西川節度使。

translations.literal: On wushen, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Chief Minister Li Guyan was made Associate Chief Minister and filled the post of Xichuan Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Wushen: vice director of the Chancellery and associate chief minister Li Guyan was kept as associate chief minister and sent out as military governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，御史台奏蕭弘詐妄。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the Censorate reported that Xiao Hong's claim was fraudulent.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayin: the Censorate reported that Xiao Hong's claim was fraudulent.

sentences.zh: 詔遞歸鄉里，不之罪，冀得其真。

translations.literal: An edict had him escorted back to his home district without punishment, hoping to obtain the truth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent him home unpunished, in hope that the truth might yet emerge.
